nodes.label: The GHG Protocol explicitly declines to require additionality

attrs.missing_or_defect: This is the canonical textual defence of annual, unbundled procurement, and it is a deliberate design position: scope 2 is an attributional allocation system, so importing an offset-style additionality test is a category error. Critics of RECs almost never engage with this sentence.
attrs.remedy: Teach this alongside the critiques. The disagreement is about what kind of object a scope 2 number is, not about whether anyone is cheating.
attrs.ground_contact: verbatim section 8.2: 'This guidance does not require contractual instruments claimed in scope 2 to be "in addition to," or independent from, regulatory policies such as subsidies, tax exemptions, or supplier quotas. Due to the design of renewable energy production targets, achieving "regulatory surplus" with voluntary purchases may not always be possible.'

nodes.label: RE100 states there is no mandatory 24/7 time-matching requirement
nodes.source_location: RE100 2026 Reporting Guidance, section on column 10 (time-matching basis)

attrs.missing_or_defect: The largest corporate renewable-electricity initiative requires annual matching only, while adding hourly matching as a DISCLOSURE field. Disclosure without a threshold is the standard way a contested requirement gets deferred.
attrs.remedy: A '100% RE100' claim is an annual claim. Ask for the column 10 time-matching basis.
attrs.ground_contact: verbatim: 'This indicates the time interval between when low-carbon electricity is generated and when it is consumed. There is no mandatory 24/7 time-matching requirement for RE100 reporting companies. However, RE100 recognizes hourly matching as an emerging high-quality procurement practice, which is why this disclosure field has been incorporated into the 2026 CDP questionnaire.'

nodes.label: The Scope 2 argument is three-way, not two-way
nodes.source_location: Brander, Gillenwater & Ascui, Energy Policy 112:29-33 (2018), CC-BY full text

attrs.missing_or_defect: Secondary sources routinely collapse this into '24/7 versus annual'. There are at least three positions: abolish the market-based method entirely (Brander); match hourly and locally (24/7 CFE); maximise marginal displacement wherever it is largest, even outside your boundary (Emissions First/CEBA). The second and third are directly opposed on locality.
attrs.remedy: Name which of the three a source is arguing for before treating it as agreement or disagreement with another.
attrs.ground_contact: verbatim: 'The fundamental issue with the contractual method is that it does not represent any causal relationship between the reporting entity and the emissions reported.' Their prescribed remedy is verbatim: 'The locational grid average method should be the only method used to calculate and report scope 2 emissions.' This is NOT the 24/7 position. Separately, the Emissions First / CEBA position attacks the LOCALITY constraint rather than the annual interval, arguing for maximum marginal tonnes displaced anywhere. Those secondary-source characterisations were read via a summarising fetch and are second-hand; the Brander quotes are byte-verified.

nodes.label: No US state examined requires an operator to report PUE or water draw
nodes.source_location: Virginia Chapters 623/896 (HB 496/SB 553); Oregon Chapter 323 (HB 3546); California Chapter 647 (SB 57); Texas SB 6 (89R); Minnesota 2025 1st Spec. Sess. ch. 12; JLARC Report 598

attrs.missing_or_defect: Any assumption that a US operator must report PUE or water consumption to a state is currently FALSE in all ten states examined. The US and EU regimes are not merely different in stringency; the US has no operator-facing metric reporting duty at all.
attrs.remedy: Do not budget for US state metric reporting as a compliance line item. Budget instead for the water supplier's disclosure of your volumes (Virginia, from 2027) and for interconnection disclosure (Texas, 75 MW).
attrs.ground_contact: Across the ten states examined, the two enacted recurring data-centre-specific reporting duties both fall on someone OTHER than the operator. Virginia Chapter 623, verbatim: 'Any water user required to register water withdrawal and use data pursuant to this subsection that provides water to another person offsite shall include in its report ... the total volume of potable water and, reported separately, the total volume of reclaimed water provided during each month' — the filer is the WATER SUPPLIER, the trigger is holding a DEQ air permit rather than a size threshold, and it is effective 1 January 2027. Oregon HB 3546 section 7 puts a biennial load-trend report on the Oregon PUC. California SB 57 creates a CPUC assessment (Pub. Util. Code 913.22: the commission 'may assess', and 'shall submit an assessment ... on or before January 1, 2027'). Texas SB 6 is interconnection disclosure at a 75 MW threshold, not energy or water reporting. Virginia HB 1601 and SB 1449 were both VETOED on 2025-05-02.

nodes.label: Minnesota makes the data-centre information it collects nonpublic

attrs.missing_or_defect: A state statute that collects data-centre information and then classifies it as nonpublic is the inverse of a transparency regime. Its existence is often cited as evidence that US states are moving toward disclosure; the text moves the other way.
attrs.remedy: Read the disclosure clause, not the headline. Collection and publication are different legislative choices and states are making them independently.
attrs.ground_contact: verbatim: 'Any communication made or information exchanged under this subdivision between a data center and a government agency, or between government agencies, is nonpublic data, as defined in section 13.02, subdivision 9.' Thresholds in the same chapter: a data centre 'designed to have a load of 100 megawatts or more'; water preapplication trigger where use 'exceeds 100,000,000 gallons per year'.

nodes.label: The embodied share is a property of the assumed grid, not of the hardware
nodes.source_location: Gupta et al., HPCA 2021, section V and Figure 13

attrs.missing_or_defect: The same hardware swings from ~40% manufacturing to >80% manufacturing purely by changing the assumed generation mix. An 'X% embodied' citation without the assumed grid AND the boundary is uninterpretable. TERMINOLOGY NOTE: this paper never uses the word 'embodied' — it says 'manufacturing' throughout.
attrs.remedy: Demand three things with any embodied-carbon percentage: the boundary, the assumed grid carbon intensity, and whether Scope 2 was location- or market-based.
attrs.ground_contact: verbatim: 'For the baseline, assuming the US energy grid, roughly 60% of Intel's carbon emissions and 45% of AMD's come from hardware use and energy consumption.' verbatim: 'Figure 13 shows that when using solar and wind, which frequently power data centers, over 80% of emissions come from hardware manufacturing.' The baseline grid is stated as 301 gCO2/kWh; solar 41 g and wind 11 g.

nodes.label: The best whole-facility figure puts Scope 3 at about half of data-centre carbon
nodes.source_location: Lyu et al., HotCarbon '23, 9 July 2023 (Microsoft Azure)

attrs.missing_or_defect: This is the most defensible whole-facility split found, and it is roughly 50/50 — materially less extreme than the 82/18 that circulates. It also corroborates the hourly-matching gap independently: '66% of the electricity used at Google datacenters was matched with renewable energy on an hourly basis in 2021'.
attrs.remedy: Use ~50/50 at 70-75% renewable as the planning assumption for a whole facility, not 82/18, and state the renewable share it is conditioned on.
attrs.ground_contact: verbatim: 'Our LCAs indicate that with 70-75% renewable energy, Scope 3 accounts for close to half of datacenter carbon emissions. Therefore, Scope 3 emissions and embodied carbon are important factors both currently and in the near future.' The boundary is whole-facility, covering carbon 'embedded in chips, PCBs, racks/server enclosures, and buildings'. The paper also verbatim rebuts the opposite overclaim as 'Myth 2. Research should focus only on embodied carbon, as renewable energy will eliminate operational carbon.' Exact figures are withheld: 'subject to confidentiality agreements'.

nodes.label: The EU writes the reuse control-volume rule into binding law
nodes.source_location: Annex II point 1(j); Annex III point (c)

attrs.remedy: Meter at the handoff, not at the heat exchanger, and net off any heat recirculated for self-cooling.
attrs.ground_contact: verbatim: 'only energy being reused outside the boundaries of the data centre is counted ... Reused energy shall be measured at the boundary of the data centre at the point where the energy provided is handed off to be used by the other party. If part of the waste heat is reused for cooling the data centre, that part must be subtracted from the reused waste heat'. ERF = E_REUSE/E_DC.

nodes.label: Waste-heat temperature is a required EU indicator because MWh alone hides usability

attrs.remedy: Treat T_WH as the design variable that decides whether reuse is possible at all. Specify the return temperature target with the offtaker before the cooling architecture is frozen.
attrs.ground_contact: verbatim: T_WH 'shall be measured as the temperature of the fluid used to cool the information and communication technology equipment in the data centre computer room, averaged over the year, and across every measurement point ... measured at the point where the heated fluid enters the heat exchanger(s) at the data centre computer room boundary'.

nodes.label: Germany had to move the PUE boundary to stop heat reuse breaking the PUE cap

attrs.missing_or_defect: Heat-pump electricity sits inside the facility boundary, so reusing heat raises PUE while raising ERF. A national legislature had to carve the boundary explicitly because the two metrics it was mandating pointed in opposite directions.
attrs.remedy: This is the definitive proof that the boundary is not a technicality. Use it as the teaching case. And check the boundary convention before comparing a heat-reusing site's PUE to anyone's.
attrs.ground_contact: verbatim: 'Bei der Berechnung der Energieverbrauchseffektivität nach Satz 1 Nummer 1 bleibt der Stromeinsatz von Anlagen, die ausschliesslich der Aufwertung der Abwaerme des Rechenzentrums dienen, unberuecksichtigt.' (In calculating PUE under sentence 1 no. 1, the electricity used by plant serving exclusively to upgrade the data centre's waste heat is disregarded.)

nodes.label: Heat reuse succeeds or fails on a counterparty the operator does not control
nodes.source_location: EnEfG section 11(3); read with Directive (EU) 2023/1791 Article 26(6)

attrs.missing_or_defect: Every escape clause is about the heat network, not the data centre. Where dense municipal heat networks exist and are compelled to engage, ERF is achievable; where they do not, the statutory duty evaporates by its own terms and no design effort changes the outcome.
attrs.remedy: Treat 'is there a heat offtaker within economic pipe distance, and is it obliged to talk to us' as a SITING input on par with grid capacity, not a sustainability add-on.
attrs.ground_contact: verbatim EED Art. 26(6): 'Member States shall ensure that data centres with a total rated energy input exceeding 1 MW utilise the waste heat or other waste heat recovery applications unless they can show that it is not technically or economically feasible'. Verbatim EnEfG section 11(3): the reuse duty falls away where (1) the share ceased to be met after commissioning through no fault of the operator; (2) an agreement with a nearby municipality or heat-network operator declares a concrete intention to build or permit a network meeting the requirement within ten years, including an investment plan, a rule on who bears the connection-line cost and the heat price; or (3) the nearby network operator fails to accept within six months an offer of reused energy at cost while the data centre holds a handover station ready. The network operator must tell the data centre its network capacity.

nodes.label: EU data-centre reporting binds at 500 kW installed IT power from 15 May 2024

attrs.missing_or_defect: Art. 12(5) makes binding EU-level PUE floors a scheduled possibility, not a speculation, and whether that report has landed was not established here.
attrs.remedy: Re-check the Article 12(5) report before assuming EU performance standards are voluntary.
attrs.ground_contact: verbatim Art. 12(1): 'By 15 May 2024 and every year thereafter, Member States shall require owners and operators of data centres in their territory with a power demand of the installed information technology (IT) of at least 500kW, to make the information set out in Annex VII publicly available, except for information subject to Union and national law protecting trade and business secrets and confidentiality.' Annex VII requires the data centre name, owner and operator names, start date, municipality, floor area, installed power, data traffic, stored/processed data, and last-full-year KPI performance on energy consumption, power utilisation, temperature set points, waste heat utilisation, water usage and renewable energy. Art. 12(2) exempts defence and civil protection. Art. 12(4) only ENCOURAGES sites at or above 1 MW to follow the EU Code of Conduct. Art. 12(5) required a Commission assessment by 15 May 2025 'accompanied, where appropriate, by legislative proposals ... including establishing minimum performance standards'.

nodes.label: The EU's first reporting year is self-selected by an explicit derogation

attrs.missing_or_defect: Points 1(d), 1(e), 1(h)-(l) and 1(o)-(r) are precisely total energy, IT energy, water, waste heat, temperatures and all three renewable categories — i.e. everything the scheme exists to collect.
attrs.remedy: Do not treat the first EU dataset as a population. Ask what fraction of respondents omitted each KPI before using it as a benchmark.
attrs.ground_contact: verbatim Art. 3(1): 'By 15 September 2024, then by 15 May 2025, and every year thereafter, reporting data centre operators shall communicate to the European database'. Verbatim Art. 3(2): 'For the first reporting period, if a data centre operator cannot monitor and gather one or more of the key performance indicators set out in Annex II, points 1(d), 1(e), 1(h)-(l), and 1(o)-(r), for technical reasons, the data centre operator may omit this information explaining the reasons for this omission.'

nodes.label: No jurisdiction found requires an independent audit of a reported PUE, WUE, ERF or REF value
nodes.source_location: Articles 1-5 and Annexes II-IV of Reg. (EU) 2024/1364, read in full; cross-read against Reg. (EU) 2021/2139 Annex I section 8.1 and EnEfG section 12

attrs.missing_or_defect: This is the answer to 'who checks it': nobody checks the number. Operators self-report, the first year is derogable, and the European record is sealed.
attrs.remedy: If you need a trustworthy PUE from a counterparty, buy it contractually: define the level, the averaging window and an independent verifier in the colocation or acquisition agreement. No regulator will do it for you.
attrs.ground_contact: Reading the full delegated regulation: there is no audit, no assurance, no third-party check and no penalty provision. The Taxonomy's third-party verification (verbatim: 'The implementation of those practices is verified by an independent third-party and audited at least every three years') attaches to PRACTICES, not to metric values. EnEfG section 12(3) requires 'Validierung oder Zertifizierung des Energie- oder Umweltmanagementsystems' — certification of the management SYSTEM, not of the numbers it produces.

nodes.label: The European database is sealed at facility level and published only in aggregate

attrs.missing_or_defect: Energy-weighted averaging means the Union's average PUE is dominated by the largest, most efficient facilities and says nothing about the median facility.
attrs.remedy: Use the EU aggregate for market context only, and read it as an energy-weighted mean, not a typical value.
attrs.ground_contact: verbatim Art. 5(5): 'The Commission and Member States concerned shall keep confidential all information and key performance indicators for individual data centres'. Annex IV publishes, at Member State and Union level only: facility counts, size distribution, total PD_IT, total E_DC, total W_IN and average PUE, WUE, ERF and REF — 'the aggregation of the sustainability indicators shall be performed with a weighted metric aggregation, using the total energy consumption as the weighting factor' — with per-category presentation 'possible only if the respective category contains data from at least three data centres'. Size bands: very small 100-500 kW, small 500-1000 kW, medium 1-2 MW, large 2-10 MW, very large >10 MW.

nodes.label: The EU Taxonomy sets no PUE, WUE or carbon threshold for data centres
nodes.source_location: Annex I section 8.1, 'Data processing, hosting and related activities'

attrs.missing_or_defect: The only numeric bar is refrigerant GWP <= 675. Taxonomy alignment is a practice-conformance audit, not a performance number — while the EED scheme collects performance numbers and verifies nothing. The two EU regimes miss each other.
attrs.remedy: Budget for the third-party CoC practice audit as a financing prerequisite, separately from the EED metering scope. They are different work.
attrs.ground_contact: verbatim substantial-contribution criteria: 'The activity has implemented all relevant practices listed as expected practices in the most recent version of the European Code of Conduct on Data Centre Energy Efficiency, or in CEN-CENELEC document CLC TR50600-99-1 ... The implementation of those practices is verified by an independent third-party and audited at least every three years.' and 'The global warming potential (GWP) of refrigerants used in the data centre cooling system does not exceed 675.' The activity is classified as a transitional activity under Art. 10(2) of Reg. (EU) 2020/852.

nodes.label: The Taxonomy states the same data-centre criterion at two stringency levels
nodes.source_location: Annex I section 8.1 versus Annex II section 8.1

attrs.missing_or_defect: Same activity, same regulation, two bars, depending on which environmental objective is claimed against — and the adaptation route has no stated third-party verification requirement.
attrs.remedy: Decide early which objective you are claiming alignment under; it changes the audit scope.
attrs.ground_contact: verbatim Annex I (mitigation, substantial contribution): 'The activity has implemented all relevant practices listed as expected practices ... verified by an independent third-party and audited at least every three years.' Verbatim Annex II (adaptation, mitigation as DNSH): 'The activity has demonstrated best efforts to implement the relevant practices listed as expected practices ... and has implemented all expected practices that have been assigned the maximum value of 5'.

nodes.label: Germany imposes binding PUE caps and heat-reuse quotas on data centres

attrs.missing_or_defect: Dates read on 2026-08-13 from the consolidated text; whether they were amended from the as-promulgated dates was NOT established. Rule 7 applies.
attrs.remedy: If any part of the campus is in Germany, PUE 1.2 and ERF 10-20% are hard design constraints, not aspirations, and they bind on the commissioning date band.
attrs.ground_contact: verbatim section 11(1): data centres commissioned before 1 July 2026 must permanently achieve, as an annual average, an Energieverbrauchseffektivitaet <= 1.5 from 1 July 2027 and <= 1.3 from 1 July 2030. Verbatim section 11(2): data centres commissioned from 1 July 2026 must achieve <= 1.2 and a reused-energy share of at least 10 percent per DIN EN 50600-4-6 (November 2020 edition); from 1 July 2027 a PLANNED reuse share of at least 15 percent; from 1 July 2028 at least 20 percent. Requirements must be met within two years of commissioning, as a permanent annual average.

nodes.label: German law accepts a 'planned' reuse share for the 2027 and 2028 cohorts
nodes.source_location: EnEfG section 11(2), second and third clauses

attrs.missing_or_defect: A design-stage number written into a binding requirement is the design-versus-demonstrated trap encoded in statute. Enforcement against a 'planned' share is a different exercise from enforcement against a measured one.
attrs.remedy: Do not read the 15%/20% cohorts as measured-performance obligations without checking how the enforcing authority treats 'geplant'.
attrs.ground_contact: verbatim: 'Rechenzentren, die ab dem 1. Juli 2027 den Betrieb aufnehmen, muessen einen geplanten Anteil an wiederverwendeter Energie von mindestens 15 Prozent aufweisen' — a GEPLANTER (planned) share, in contrast to the 2026 cohort's unqualified requirement.

nodes.label: Germany publishes per-facility named metrics while the EU seals the same numbers

attrs.missing_or_defect: The same indicators are named-and-published in Germany and confidential in the European database. Whether a competitor's PUE is legible depends on the Member State.
attrs.remedy: For German assets, assume your PUE, reuse share and WUE will be public with your name on them. Price that into the design decision, not into the communications plan.
attrs.ground_contact: verbatim section 13(1): operators must, by the end of 31 March each year, publish and transmit to the federal government the Anlage 3 information for the preceding calendar year. Anlage 3 requires: the data centre name; owner and operator names; size class by IT connected load (<500 kW, <1 MW, <5 MW, <10 MW, <50 MW, <100 MW, >=100 MW); postcode; total building area; rated IT connected load and non-redundant rated load; total electricity consumption including self-generation, total purchased electricity and electricity fed back; renewable share per DIN EN 50600-4-3 (Nov 2020); quantity and average temperature of waste heat rejected to air, water or ground; quantity and average temperature of waste heat delivered to offtakers; data stored and processed; PUE per DIN EN 50600-4-2 (Aug 2019); reuse share per DIN EN 50600-4-6 (Nov 2020); cooling system efficiency per DIN EN 50600-4-7 (Aug 2020); water-use efficiency per 'DIN EN 50600-9, Ausgabe Mai 2020' (cited exactly as printed).

nodes.label: German law certifies the management system, not the metric

attrs.missing_or_defect: Certification of an ISO 50001-style system is not verification of a PUE value. The strongest assurance requirement found still does not attest the number.
attrs.remedy: Do not accept 'our EnMS is certified' as evidence that a published PUE is correct.
attrs.ground_contact: verbatim: an energy or environmental management system was required by 1 July 2025; it must include 'kontinuierliche Messungen zur elektrischen Leistung und zum Energiebedarf der wesentlichen Komponenten des Rechenzentrums'; validation or certification of that system is mandatory from 1 January 2026 for data centres with non-redundant rated connected load from 1 MW (300 kW where publicly owned or operated) and for IT operators from 500 kW (300 kW public). Exemption where at least 50 percent of the reused energy is taken via a heat network and the three-year average total final energy does not exceed 7.5 GWh.

nodes.label: Two standard families define the same metrics, and EU and German law both pick the European one
nodes.source_location: ISO free catalogue listing, read against Reg. (EU) 2024/1364 Annex II and EnEfG Anlage 3

attrs.missing_or_defect: Whether the ISO and EN definitions of the same metric agree is UNVERIFIED — both are paywalled and neither was read. A global operator may hold two differently-defined PUEs for one asset.
attrs.remedy: Pin the standard family AND the edition year in every contract that references a metric. Do not assume ISO/IEC 30134-2 and EN 50600-4-2 are interchangeable.
attrs.ground_contact: ISO/IEC 30134 parts 2 (PUE), 3 (REF), 6 (ERF), 7 (CER), 8 (CUE), 9 (WUE) cover the same metrics as CEN/CENELEC EN 50600-4-2/-4-3/-4-6/-4-7/-4-9. Reg. (EU) 2024/1364 and EnEfG Anlage 3 both reference EN 50600, not ISO/IEC 30134. ISO/IEC 30134-2 moved to a second edition in 2026-01 (2016 edition withdrawn); parts 6 and 9 are under revision.

nodes.label: The primary definitions of WUE, CUE and ERE are now behind a membership login
nodes.source_location: The Green Grid About Us page; ITI news release 3 November 2025

attrs.missing_or_defect: A metric that regulators reference and the industry quotes daily has no freely readable authoritative definition — the free copies are mirrors and archives that could disappear.
attrs.remedy: Archive local copies of WP#29, #32, #35 and #49 now, with capture dates, before citing them in any course or contract.
attrs.ground_contact: verbatim TGG: 'The Green Grid was founded in 2007 ... In 2019 TGG was acquired as an affiliate member of the Information Technology Industry Council (ITI) ... TGG continues to serve and advocate for the data center industry'. The WP#29/#32/#35 PDFs at the original thegreengrid.org URLs are dead; the current library pages require sign-in to download. The verbatim text used in this fragment came from a third-party mirror and from Internet Archive captures.

nodes.label: SINGLE-SOURCED: 'the industry average PUE is about 1.55'
nodes.source_location: Google's citation of Uptime Institute; Uptime Institute Journal 2023-12-04

attrs.missing_or_defect: Repetition is not corroboration. It is one self-reported, unweighted, respondent-composition-dependent survey, quoted by many parties, with no boundary or category disclosed for any respondent's figure.
attrs.remedy: Cite it as 'Uptime survey respondents' self-reported average', never as 'the industry average'. Do not treat multiple citations of it as multiple sources.
attrs.ground_contact: Google states verbatim: 'According to the Uptime Institute's 2025 Global Data Center Survey, the global average PUE of respondents' data centers was 1.54.' Every instance of this figure I could follow traces back to the SAME self-reported Uptime survey, including Google's own use of it.

nodes.label: CONTESTED: the water intensity of US electricity is 1.8 L/kWh
nodes.source_location: The Green Grid WP#35 Appendix A, default EWIF table (2011)

attrs.missing_or_defect: Contradicted by LBNL 2024's 4.35 L/kWh US average. Provenance now established: the 1.8 figure is NREL/TP-550-33905 (Torcellini et al., December 2003), which is THERMOELECTRIC-ONLY and per kWh at the point of end use; the same NREL sentence gives hydro 68 L/kWh and a national weighted thermoelectric-plus-hydro average of 7.6 L/kWh. TGG adopted the thermoelectric-only number as a national average AND separately set hydro to 0, excluding hydro twice.
attrs.remedy: Do not use the 2011 EWIF defaults for a 2026 decision. Compute EWIF from balancing-authority data and state whether reservoir evaporation is included.
attrs.ground_contact: verbatim TGG defaults: Hydro 0, Solar PV 0, Wind 0, Concentrated Solar 3.3, Coal 2.2, Nuclear 3.3, Natural Gas 0.8, Unknown 1.8 L/kWh, 'Per the U.S. Aggregate for Thermoelectric Plants'.

nodes.label: DATED, UNVERIFIED HISTORY: EnEfG PUE caps take effect 1 July 2027 and 1 July 2030
nodes.source_location: EnEfG section 11(1), consolidated text as displayed on 2026-08-13

attrs.missing_or_defect: A binding compliance deadline whose amendment history is unverified is exactly the kind of figure that ages badly.
attrs.remedy: Re-read the consolidated text on the day you quote it, and check the BGBl amendment chain.
attrs.ground_contact: The dates were read verbatim from the consolidated statutory text on 2026-08-13. Whether section 11(1) was amended from the dates as originally promulgated on 2023-11-13 was NOT established — the gesetze-im-internet index page did not expose an amendment history to the fetch used.

nodes.label: Curricula teach the PUE ratio and omit the boundary, interval and category

attrs.missing_or_defect: A learner who answers every PUE item correctly still cannot say where the IT meter is, over what window, or whether the number was measured at all.
attrs.remedy: Add apply/evaluate items keyed on the level table (UPS/PDU/IT-input x monthly/daily/continuous) and on the PUE_{a,b} subscript. Require quantity_evidence other than qualitative_only.
attrs.ground_contact: MEASURED: 53 of 804 items mention PUE; ZERO mention measurement boundary, control volume, PUE category or level, UPS-output versus PDU-output versus IT-input metering, annualised/trailing-twelve-month averaging, design versus demonstrated, or partial load. All 53 PUE items carry quantity_evidence = 'qualitative_only' — not one requires a calculation with a real number. The two canonical definition items (m06-q021, m06-q100) are the same question with options shuffled, both bloom = 'remember', both explaining only 'PUE = total facility energy / IT energy; lower overhead is better.'

nodes.label: There is no taught procedure for interrogating a published PUE claim

attrs.missing_or_defect: Interrogation is the actual professional skill and it is entirely absent.
attrs.remedy: Teach the nineteen-lever checklist as a procedure with a question per lever, and assess it with scenario items where the trap is the boundary, not the arithmetic.
attrs.ground_contact: MEASURED: zero items on design-vs-demonstrated, partial load, seasonality, fleet composition, pPUE, or source-energy weighting. The bank has items warning that a good PUE does not imply availability, but none that interrogate the PUE number itself.

nodes.label: The metric family beyond PUE and WUE is completely absent

attrs.missing_or_defect: CUE, ERE, ERF and REF are the metrics that EU and German law actually mandate, and none appears.
attrs.remedy: Add a metric-family module: the table of eight metrics with formula, units and range, plus ERE = (1-ERF) x PUE and CUE = CEF x PUE as computational items.
attrs.ground_contact: MEASURED (case-sensitive): PUE 53 items, WUE 4 items, CUE 0, ERE 0, ERF 0, 'energy reuse' 0, 'heat reuse'/'waste heat' 0. The four WUE items are definitional and two of them are the same item.

nodes.label: Carbon accounting is absent from the bank entirely

attrs.missing_or_defect: The single most consequential and most contested area of the domain is not represented by one question.
attrs.remedy: Teach dual reporting, the eight Scope 2 Quality Criteria verbatim, and the vintage/market-boundary commentary that generates the 24/7 argument.
attrs.ground_contact: MEASURED: zero items mention scope 2, scope 3, market-based, location-based, renewable energy certificates, guarantees of origin, eGRID or emission factors.

nodes.label: No item touches any reporting regime

attrs.missing_or_defect: An operator at 500 kW installed IT power in the EU has had a legal reporting duty since 15 May 2024 and a learner would not know it exists.
attrs.remedy: Add regime items with the thresholds and dates as the assessed content: 500 kW, 15 May annually, PUE/WUE/ERF/REF, aggregate-only publication, and the German per-facility publication contrast.
attrs.ground_contact: MEASURED: zero items match 'reporting requirement' or 'disclosure'. Legal/regulatory content in the bank is generic.

nodes.label: The site-versus-source distinction is untaught and it is an order of magnitude

attrs.missing_or_defect: The bank teaches the smaller of two numbers that differ by roughly 10x, and teaches it as if it were the water footprint.
attrs.remedy: Teach WUE_source = EWIF x PUE + site WUE as a computation, with a worked example using a real balancing authority.
attrs.ground_contact: MEASURED: the four WUE items all describe 'site water use relative to IT energy' and none mentions WUE_source, EWIF, or indirect water. LBNL 2024 puts indirect water at 4.52 L/kWh against a site WUE just over 0.36 L/kWh.

nodes.label: Nobody teaches that none of these numbers is independently verified
nodes.source_location: Reg. (EU) 2024/1364 read in full; EnEfG section 12; Reg. (EU) 2021/2139 Annex I section 8.1

attrs.missing_or_defect: Learners are taught metrics as if they were measurements produced by a system with checks. There is no such system.
attrs.remedy: Teach 'who verifies this' as a standing question with the answer 'nobody, unless you write it into a contract'. Then teach how to write it into a contract.
attrs.ground_contact: Reading all three: no assurance requirement attaches to any reported metric value anywhere. The Taxonomy audits practices; Germany certifies the management system; the EU database is self-reported and sealed.

nodes.label: CUE is standardised and orphaned — defined, ISO-published, mandated nowhere
nodes.source_location: recital 192 of Directive (EU) 2023/1791 against Annex III of Reg. (EU) 2024/1364; ISO free catalogue

attrs.missing_or_defect: The one metric in the family that expresses carbon is the one nobody has to report, which is why operators publish REF instead.
attrs.remedy: Teach why: REF is a procurement disclosure that can be bought; CUE is a consumption disclosure that cannot. Then teach learners to ask for the location-based Scope 2 number instead.
attrs.ground_contact: The Directive's recital names carbon usage effectiveness; the delegated act's Annex III defines only PUE, WUE, ERF, REF. ISO/IEC 30134-8:2022 exists (title and date read from the free catalogue). No regime found requires CUE.

nodes.label: No metric in force connects water volume to water scarcity
nodes.source_location: Annex III point (b) of Reg. (EU) 2024/1364; ITI release 2025-11-03

attrs.missing_or_defect: A litre in a stressed basin and a litre in a wet one are the same number in every mandatory indicator.
attrs.remedy: Pair every WUE figure with a basin stress score from an external source; do not wait for a standard to require it.
attrs.ground_contact: WUE = W_IN/E_IT contains no scarcity term. The Green Grid announced a Water Usage Impact metric on 2025-10-29 that reportedly combines consumption with local water stress; it is login-gated and unadopted by any regime.

nodes.label: No public emission factor answers what a new large load causes
nodes.source_location: eGRID frequent questions; NREL Cambium unreachable

attrs.missing_or_defect: Every campus carbon figure in circulation uses an average factor for a question averages cannot answer, and the tool that could is not in most curricula.
attrs.remedy: Teach the three-way distinction — average, short-run marginal, long-run marginal — and make the learner state which one a claim used.
attrs.ground_contact: eGRID's two rate families are scoped by EPA to existing electricity use and to displacement projects respectively. The long-run marginal dataset that would address a new large load could not be read here (nrel.gov unreachable 2026-08-13).

nodes.label: Metric definitions drift by standard edition and nobody pins the edition
nodes.source_location: ISO free catalogue; Reg. (EU) 2024/1364 Annex II; EnEfG Anlage 3

attrs.missing_or_defect: Two binding instruments pin the same metric to different (or unspecified) editions, and the ISO family moved underneath both in January 2026.
attrs.remedy: Pin standard family and edition year in every contract and every teaching artefact, and re-check annually.
attrs.ground_contact: ISO/IEC 30134-2 second edition published 2026-01, superseding the withdrawn 2016 edition and its 2018 amendment; parts 6 and 9 under revision. Reg. (EU) 2024/1364 cites 'EN 50600-4-2' with no edition; EnEfG Anlage 3 cites 'DIN EN 50600-4-2, Ausgabe August 2019'. Contents of none of these were read.

nodes.label: The binding definitions of legally mandated indicators are paywalled
nodes.source_location: Annex II of Reg. (EU) 2024/1364; EnEfG Anlage 3 footnotes

attrs.missing_or_defect: A regulated party cannot read the definition of what it is required to report without paying a private publisher. Neither can a course author, an auditor, or a community group.
attrs.remedy: Budget for the standards. And teach the boundary from the freely readable primary sources — The Green Grid WP#49 and the EU regulation's own Annex II text — which are sufficient.
attrs.ground_contact: EU and German law delegate the measurement methodology for legally mandated indicators to CEN/CENELEC EN 50600-4-x and DIN EN 50600-4-x, which are sold by Beuth Verlag and are not publicly readable. The German statute's own footnotes say so: 'Die Norm ist bei der Beuth Verlag GmbH, Berlin, erschienen'.

nodes.label: Embodied carbon sits outside every mandated data-centre metric
nodes.source_location: Gupta et al., HPCA 2021, Figure 2; read against Reg. (EU) 2024/1364 Annex III and TGG WP#32

attrs.missing_or_defect: The industry's entire mandatory measurement apparatus is pointed at the minority term of the footprint, and says so in its own founding documents.
attrs.remedy: Teach the operating/embodied split and its dependence on the Scope 2 method. Require a building-and-hardware LCA as a proposal deliverable, not a metric.
attrs.ground_contact: PUE, WUE, ERF, REF and CUE are all operating-phase metrics. WP#32 excludes lifecycle carbon by explicit design decision, verbatim: 'attempting to determine the carbon generated in the manufacturing of the IT equipment and its subsequent shipping to the data center would make the metric far too difficult to measure, calculate, or use.' Gupta et al. put capex at 82% of Facebook's 2018 data-centre footprint under market-based accounting.

nodes.label: Five US states' data-centre legislation remains unread
nodes.source_location: research gap, narrowed after Virginia, Oregon, California, Texas and Minnesota were grounded

attrs.missing_or_defect: The 'no US state requires operator metric reporting' finding is established across ten states but not proven across fifty. Georgia in particular is a major data-centre market.
attrs.remedy: Re-run for GA, WA, IL, MD, AZ and NY against legislature primary sources, recording enacted status and effective date on every entry per rule 7.
attrs.ground_contact: UNGROUNDED for Georgia (legis.ga.gov is a JavaScript app; SB 34's subject and status were never read), Washington, Illinois, Maryland and Arizona (no bill numbers discoverable without a working search engine). NOTHING is asserted about these five and NO bill number is invented. New York S10642's reported 50 MW public-disclosure threshold is second-hand via NCSL and unverified against primary source, so it is not asserted either.

nodes.label: ASHRAE 90.4 compliance paths cannot be supplied by an AI agent

attrs.missing_or_defect: The US design-side energy compliance route for a new data centre is a hole in every AI-assembled knowledge graph, including this one, and will remain one.
attrs.remedy: Assign a human with a licensed copy to write this section. Never route it through an AI tool, including via third-party summaries that quote the standard.
attrs.ground_contact: UNGROUNDED — ASHRAE AI policy prohibits ingestion of ASHRAE IP into any AI tool. This gap is recorded as a correct output of the research process, not as a research failure.

nodes.label: Specify the PUE measurement level and averaging period in the design brief

attrs.missing_or_defect: If the brief says 'PUE 1.25' with no level and no window, the delivered metering will be whatever is cheapest and the acceptance test will be unarguable.
attrs.remedy: Write: 'PUE_{L2,YC} not to exceed X, demonstrated over twelve consecutive months at not less than Y% of design IT load, IT energy metered at PDU output, total facility energy at the utility hand-off including all substation and transformer losses.' Then price the metering.
attrs.ground_contact: Grounded in the WP#49 level table and the Global Task Force's PUE_{L2,YC} recommendation.

nodes.label: Set PUE, WUE and ERF targets jointly with an explicit exchange rate

attrs.missing_or_defect: A scorecard containing PUE alone is an instruction to consume water; a scorecard containing WUE alone is an instruction to consume energy; either alone penalises heat reuse.
attrs.remedy: Publish the exchange rate you will accept — litres per kWh of PUE improvement — before the cooling architecture is frozen, and state which boundary convention applies to heat-upgrade plant.
attrs.ground_contact: Grounded in LBNL's explicit statement of the PUE/WUE trade-off and in Germany's statutory need to carve heat-pump electricity out of the PUE calculation.

nodes.label: Treat heat offtake and basin water stress as siting inputs, not sustainability add-ons

attrs.missing_or_defect: Heat reuse and water stress are usually assessed after site selection, when neither can be changed.
attrs.remedy: Add two screens to the site scorecard: distance to a heat network with statutory engagement obligations, and basin baseline water stress. Both are decided by the land purchase.
attrs.ground_contact: Grounded in the fact that every statutory escape from the heat-reuse duty turns on the existence and willingness of a nearby heat network — a factor fixed at the moment the land is chosen.

nodes.label: Buy metric assurance contractually, because no regulator supplies it
nodes.source_location: Reg. (EU) 2024/1364 Articles 1-5 read in full; EnEfG section 12(3)

attrs.missing_or_defect: Every reported PUE, WUE, ERF and REF in the market is self-attested.
attrs.remedy: Put the verifier, the boundary, the averaging window and the remedy for non-achievement into the colocation, EPC or acquisition agreement. It is the only place they exist.
attrs.ground_contact: Grounded in the absence of any assurance provision across the delegated regulation, and in the fact that the German certification obligation attaches to the management system.

nodes.label: Self-reported survey PUE and modelled national PUE disagree by about 0.14
nodes.source_location: Uptime Institute survey figures against LBNL 2024 Figure 4.6

attrs.missing_or_defect: Both are called 'average PUE' and they are not the same quantity.
attrs.remedy: State the estimator whenever you quote an average PUE: self-reported survey, unweighted, global; or modelled, server-weighted, US-only.
attrs.ground_contact: Uptime's self-reported global respondent average is 1.54 (2025 survey, as cited verbatim by Google) and was 'stuck in the 1.55 to 1.59 band' 2020-2023. LBNL's bottom-up simulation gives a US average of 1.4 for 2023.

nodes.label: L2 capacity programme and density

attrs.missing_or_defect: Wave-2 lineage: IT load forecasting and phasing, rack density trajectory, the density-to-cooling-to-water-to-utility consequence chain, stranded capacity, and the capacity arithmetic a practitioner must be able to perform. Excludes cooling technology selection (L4), interconnection queue mechanics (L1), electrical topology (L3), lead times (L6).
attrs.remedy: n/a - provenance node
attrs.ground_contact: Own deliverable; every downstream claim carries its own source_file and recorded_at.

nodes.label: Greenfield campus: land closed, IT load and density band undecided

attrs.missing_or_defect: Organising scenario. Four different MW figures - design, contract, installed, utilised - are routinely spoken as one word, and the capacity programme is the decision that separates them.
attrs.remedy: Name all four MW figures explicitly in the proposal and carry their differences as line items.
attrs.ground_contact: Scenario given by the wave brief; the four-number split is evidenced by LBNL's 50% capacity-utilisation assumption and AEP Ohio's 85% minimum billing demand.

nodes.label: Decision: contract capacity and load ramp schedule for the campus

attrs.missing_or_defect: Contract capacity is chosen before the tenant mix is known, is billed against a minimum-take floor, and is locked for a decade. It is not the design capacity and is not an engineering number.
attrs.remedy: Size contract capacity against the tariff ramp schedule and the minimum-take floor, not against design capacity; carry contract-minus-utilised MW as a financial line item for the full term.
attrs.ground_contact: AEP Ohio Schedule DCT ramp percentages and 85% minimum billing demand, read directly from the utility page 2026-08-13.

nodes.label: Decision: target rack density band for the campus

attrs.missing_or_defect: Density is chosen in a compute-procurement conversation and silently fixes rack count, white-space area, building shell, structural loading, distribution sizing and the cooling fork.
attrs.remedy: Fix a density BAND (not a point) before the building shell is committed; state the modal and frontier assumptions separately and size the shell against the band.
attrs.ground_contact: Rack count across the plausible density range varies sixteen-fold for the same IT MW - computed from LBNL server ratings and Uptime density figures.

nodes.label: Decision: the kW per rack at which this campus commits to liquid cooling

attrs.missing_or_defect: Two different thresholds - economic (rack-level capex) and physical (chip-level heat flux) - are merged into one number, so the decision is made against the wrong criterion.
attrs.remedy: State both thresholds separately in the design basis and record which one binds for this campus. Hand the technology selection itself to the cooling lineage.
attrs.ground_contact: Uptime gives 20-30 kW/rack as the economic consensus; Google states air cannot manage chips above 1000 W TDP. Both read directly.

nodes.label: US data centre electricity reached 176 TWh and 4.4% of US consumption in 2023

attrs.missing_or_defect: Verbatim: 'U.S. data center energy use has continued to grow at an increasing rate, reaching 176 TWh by 2023, representing 4.4% of total U.S. electricity consumption.' Also: about 60 TWh 2014-2016; 76 TWh and 1.9% by 2018.
attrs.remedy: Use as the dated national baseline; re-measure annually.
attrs.ground_contact: Read verbatim from the LBNL-2001637 PDF text (pdftotext) 2026-08-13.

nodes.label: LBNL projects 325 to 580 TWh of US data centre electricity in 2028

attrs.missing_or_defect: Verbatim: 'the low and high end of roughly 325 and 580 TWh in 2028'. CAGR stated as ~7% 2014-2018, 18% 2018-2023, and 13-27% 2023-2028.
attrs.remedy: Treat the range, not a midpoint, as the planning input; the width is the finding.
attrs.ground_contact: Read verbatim from LBNL-2001637 2026-08-13.

nodes.label: LBNL converts annual energy to power demand using an explicit 50% capacity utilisation assumption

attrs.missing_or_defect: Verbatim: 'Assuming an average capacity utilization rate of 50%, this annual energy use range would translate to a total power demand for data centers between 74 and 132 GW.' A federal laboratory had to invent this factor because no public source gives the real installed-versus-drawn ratio.
attrs.remedy: Teach this conversion as the defining capacity computation: GW = TWh x 1e9 / 8766 / capacity_utilisation. Never quote a TWh figure as if it were a capacity figure.
attrs.ground_contact: Read verbatim from LBNL-2001637 2026-08-13; arithmetic independently checked (325 TWh / 8766 h = 37.1 GW average; / 0.5 = 74.2 GW).

nodes.label: Rated power of 8-GPU AI server nodes by accelerator class
nodes.source_location: Section 3, Server Operational Wattage - AI Servers

attrs.missing_or_defect: Verbatim worked example: 'the NVIDIA A100 class, with a rated power of 6.5 kW ... the NVIDIA A2, A40, or L4 class, with a rated server power of 3.4 kW ... the NVIDIA H100 class ... with a rated server power of 10.2 kW, and ... the B100 class, with a rated power of 12.2 kW'. Attributed to NVIDIA and Omdia.
attrs.remedy: These are the only free, dated, citable per-node power figures found. Use them as the basis for all rack arithmetic in the curriculum.
attrs.ground_contact: Read verbatim from LBNL-2001637 2026-08-13.

nodes.label: AI server operational power is modelled at 70% of rated, varied 60-80%

attrs.missing_or_defect: Verbatim: 'we estimate that, during typical operation, the power draw for these servers is 70% of the rated power' and 'Operational power in the years 2024 to 2028 is varied between 60% and 80% of the rated power'.
attrs.remedy: Provisioning uses rated; drawing uses operational. The difference is the headroom, and whether it is headroom or waste depends on the diversity assumption.
attrs.ground_contact: Read verbatim from LBNL-2001637 2026-08-13.

nodes.label: Measured 8xH100 nodes averaged 74% of rated TDP in training workload
nodes.source_location: Section 3, Server Operational Wattage - AI Servers

attrs.missing_or_defect: Verbatim: 'across both single-node and multi-node AI training workloads, 8 H100 GPU nodes averaged 74% of manufacturer rated thermal design power in workload' (citing Newkirk 2024).
attrs.remedy: This is the rare case where a nameplate-to-measured ratio is published. Use it to teach that nameplate is not a load.
attrs.ground_contact: Read verbatim from LBNL-2001637 2026-08-13.

nodes.label: Conventional dual-processor server operational wattage: 600 W in 2023 rising to 782 W by 2028

attrs.missing_or_defect: Verbatim: 'the operational wattage of dual processor servers is set to 600 W based on the Green Grid Server Energy Efficiency Database (SEED) average for that year ... ultimately reaching 782 W by 2028'. Pre-2014 volume 1S/2S maxima were 118 W and 365 W.
attrs.remedy: Gives the non-AI half of a mixed-density campus its arithmetic basis.
attrs.ground_contact: Read verbatim from LBNL-2001637 2026-08-13.

nodes.label: Server utilisation differs three-fold by facility type and is rising

attrs.missing_or_defect: Verbatim: 'Servers in internal and small data centers average 11% utilization in 2014, rising linearly to 20% in 2027. Colocation data centers average 21% utilization in 2014, rising to 35% in 2027. Hyperscale data centers average 45% in 2014, rising to 50% in 2027.'
attrs.remedy: Utilisation is a property of the operator, not of the building. A campus's utilised-versus-installed ratio is set by who signs the lease.
attrs.ground_contact: Read verbatim from LBNL-2001637 2026-08-13.

nodes.label: AI training servers are modelled at 80% operational time, inference at 40%

attrs.missing_or_defect: Verbatim: 'AI accelerated and non-accelerated servers doing training are assumed to have a constant 80% operational time throughout the whole period, while the same servers doing inferencing have a constant 40% operational time'.
attrs.remedy: The training-versus-inference split doubles or halves the utilised load for identical installed capacity. It belongs in the capacity forecast, not only in the compute plan.
attrs.ground_contact: Read verbatim from LBNL-2001637 2026-08-13.

nodes.label: Modelled US average PUE fell from 1.6 in 2014 to 1.4 in 2023 and is projected at 1.15-1.35 by 2028

attrs.missing_or_defect: Verbatim: 'The resulting annual average PUE falls from 1.6 in 2014 to 1.4 in 2023 ... by 2028, the average PUE falls to between 1.15 and 1.35'. This is a modelled national installed-stock average, not a design basis.
attrs.remedy: Use PUE to convert IT MW to facility MW for utility service sizing; never use a national average as a design target.
attrs.ground_contact: Read verbatim from LBNL-2001637 2026-08-13.

nodes.label: LBNL states its simulated PUEs assume commissioning that rarely happens

attrs.missing_or_defect: Verbatim: 'Note that simulated PUEs assume systems are commissioned and operate as designed. This is rarely the case, and generally system performance does not meet design expectations ... Therefore, the actual PUEs (and WUEs) will likely not be as good as estimated.'
attrs.remedy: A modelled efficiency figure is an upper bound on as-operated performance. Budget the commissioning gap explicitly rather than inheriting the model's optimism.
attrs.ground_contact: Read verbatim from LBNL-2001637 2026-08-13.

nodes.label: Modelled US average site WUE just over 0.36 L/kWh through 2023, rising to 0.45-0.48 by 2028

attrs.missing_or_defect: Verbatim: 'the overall average WUE, which stays just over 0.36 L/kWh through 2023 ... After 2023, the average WUE rises slightly, reaching between 0.45 and 0.48 L/kWh, reflecting increasing WUEs in the hyperscale and colocation data centers, along with the increased water consumption of liquid-cooled systems.'
attrs.remedy: Note the direction: LBNL models liquid cooling as INCREASING average water use, which contradicts the common assumption that liquid saves water.
attrs.ground_contact: Read verbatim from LBNL-2001637 2026-08-13.

nodes.label: LBNL defines WUE as water CONSUMPTION per IT kWh, distinguishing site from source

attrs.missing_or_defect: Verbatim: 'Water Usage Effectiveness is similarly defined as the total water consumption of the data center divided by the electricity demand of the IT equipment ... on-site (or "direct") water consumption, sometimes referred to as "WUE (site)" ... as opposed to the water consumption from the electricity generation ("WUE (source)").'
attrs.remedy: Every WUE figure must be tagged consumption-or-withdrawal and site-or-source before it is compared to any other WUE figure. Identical units hide incompatible numerators.
attrs.ground_contact: Read verbatim from LBNL-2001637 2026-08-13.

nodes.label: LBNL flags its own hyperscale water model as possibly too low

attrs.missing_or_defect: Verbatim: 'This optimal operation might not be reflective of the true practices with these systems, and therefore the WUE of this system ... may be low. Some hyperscale facilities report WUE values for similar systems of 0.1-0.3 L/kWh, which is much higher than the values simulated here, though the specifics of those systems are not known.'
attrs.remedy: A federal laboratory publicly distrusting its own figure is stronger evidence than the figure. Do not underwrite a modelled water floor.
attrs.ground_contact: Read verbatim from LBNL-2001637 2026-08-13.

nodes.label: US data centre direct water consumption grew from 21.2 to 66 billion litres between 2014 and 2023

attrs.missing_or_defect: Verbatim: 'In 2014, data centers consumed 21.2 billion liters of water, with 64% in internal data centers. By 2023, hyperscale and colocation account for 84% of the 66-billion-liter total ... Hyperscale data centers in 2028 are expected to consume between 60 and 124 billion liters.'
attrs.remedy: Water demand tracks the density and cooling decisions, and the growth is concentrated in exactly the facility class a new campus will be.
attrs.ground_contact: Read verbatim from LBNL-2001637 2026-08-13.

nodes.label: Indirect (generation-side) water intensity for US data centres is 4.52 L/kWh, an order of magnitude above site WUE

attrs.missing_or_defect: Verbatim: 'The total indirect water footprint of U.S. data centers is nearly 800 billion liters ... In 2023, energy consumption by a data center translates to national average of 4.52 L/kWh of indirect water consumption ... In comparison, the average water intensity factor for electricity use in the U.S. overall is 4.35 L/kWh.' LBNL notes the method excludes PPAs and behind-the-meter generation.
attrs.remedy: Site WUE (0.36 L/kWh) is roughly one-twelfth of the generation-side water the same load causes. A campus optimising site WUE alone is optimising the small term.
attrs.ground_contact: Read verbatim from LBNL-2001637 2026-08-13.

nodes.label: LBNL's national model is built from rack counts but publishes no kW per rack
nodes.source_location: Section 4, Distribution of Servers Across Data Center Types

attrs.missing_or_defect: The model uses 'an IDC "build" dataset that includes number of racks in each space type, plus an estimate of how many servers are typically on each rack in various data center types'. Racks are an internal variable; no rack power density figure appears anywhere in the report.
attrs.remedy: Stop expecting the authoritative national energy study to supply a kW/rack figure. It does not, and the gap must be filled from survey and vendor sources with their own provenance.
attrs.ground_contact: Searched the full extracted text of LBNL-2001637 for 'kW per rack', 'kW/rack', 'rack density', 'rack power' - zero matches, 2026-08-13.

nodes.label: LBNL extrapolated rack-scale AI system power linearly because vendor figures were unavailable

attrs.missing_or_defect: Verbatim: 'Larger-scale AI server configurations have been announced, namely the 72-GPU rack-scale GB200 from NVIDIA ... but these are not yet being deployed and the power draw of these systems is expected to scale close to linearly from 8-GPU machines.'
attrs.remedy: Any circulating 'GB200 NVL72 draws N kW' figure must be traced to a primary vendor document before use; LBNL could not obtain one either.
attrs.ground_contact: Read verbatim from LBNL-2001637 2026-08-13.

nodes.label: NVIDIA does not publish a rack power figure for GB200 NVL72 on its product page

attrs.missing_or_defect: The page states '36 Grace CPUs and 72 Blackwell GPUs in a rack-scale, liquid-cooled design' and gives memory, NVLink bandwidth and core counts, but no kW rack power and no rack weight. Fetched 2026-08-13.
attrs.remedy: Record the absence rather than importing a secondary figure. If a rack power number is needed contractually, obtain it from the vendor in writing.
attrs.ground_contact: Fetched directly 2026-08-13; kW figure confirmed ABSENT from the page.

nodes.label: NVIDIA's GB300 NVL72 page states performance per megawatt but no absolute rack power

attrs.missing_or_defect: The page gives 'a 5x improvement in throughput (TPS per megawatt (MW))' and 'up to a 50x overall increase in AI factory output performance', both RELATIVE metrics. No absolute kW or MW rack draw appears. Fetched 2026-08-13.
attrs.remedy: A per-megawatt efficiency ratio cannot be used to size a substation. Require the absolute figure as a contract deliverable.
attrs.ground_contact: Fetched directly 2026-08-13; absence of an absolute figure confirmed on the page.

nodes.label: The circulating 'GB200 NVL72 draws about 60 kW per rack' figure is unsourced

attrs.missing_or_defect: The figure appears widely in analyst commentary and infrastructure blogs. Two independent research passes in this session failed to trace it to any NVIDIA document, OCP specification or peer-reviewed source; NVIDIA's own GB200 and GB300 pages publish no absolute rack power; and LBNL, building the national model, extrapolated linearly rather than citing a figure.
attrs.remedy: Record as UNSOURCED and REJECT downstream. Per rule 5, two independent lineages hitting the same untraceable number is circulation, not corroboration - the repetition must not raise its confidence.
attrs.ground_contact: UNGROUNDED - no primary source located. The absence was verified positively against both NVIDIA product pages 2026-08-13.

nodes.label: Open Compute Project specifications were not retrievable in this pass

attrs.missing_or_defect: Every attempted opencompute.org path returned HTTP 403 during this session, so Open Rack v3 busbar ratings, power-shelf capacity and the 800 VDC target rack power could not be read. Circulating figures for those specifications ('ORV3 400A/800A at 48V', 'Mt Diablo 1-2 MW per rack') are UNSOURCED here.
attrs.remedy: Retrieve the OCP specifications through a route that works and re-record; do not quote the circulating values in the interim.
attrs.ground_contact: UNGROUNDED - 403 on every attempted OCP URL 2026-08-13. Recorded as an access failure, not as evidence about OCP's contents.

nodes.label: Modal rack density is shifting toward 10 kW with over a quarter of operators above it
nodes.source_location: Daniel Bizo, 2026-07-29, citing Uptime Global Data Center Survey 2025

attrs.missing_or_defect: Verbatim: 'Typical (modal) rack densities are now shifting toward 10 kW with more than a quarter of operators reporting densities above this threshold'. This is a survey of self-selected respondents describing the INSTALLED BASE.
attrs.remedy: Use as the installed-base anchor. Never use it as the design basis for an AI campus, and never let a frontier figure replace it when describing the existing estate.
attrs.ground_contact: Fetched and quoted directly 2026-08-13.

nodes.label: Direct liquid cooling becomes economically justified in the 20-30 kW per rack range

attrs.missing_or_defect: Verbatim: 'from around 20-25 kW per rack, overall capital cost gains start to thin out' and 'the industry consensus falls in the 20-30 kW per rack range'. This is an ECONOMIC threshold at rack level, not a physical limit.
attrs.remedy: Carry as the economic leg of the air-liquid fork and label it as such.
attrs.ground_contact: Fetched and quoted directly 2026-08-13.

nodes.label: Direct liquid cooling adds roughly 5-10% capital expenditure for new builds

attrs.missing_or_defect: Verbatim: 'Uptime Institute's cost estimates reveal that, on balance, this premium can amount to roughly 5-10% in capital expenditure for new builds'.
attrs.remedy: A capex delta this size is decided at density selection, years before the cooling vendor is chosen.
attrs.ground_contact: Fetched and quoted directly 2026-08-13.

nodes.label: Raising density collapses thermal ride-through from tens of minutes to seconds

attrs.missing_or_defect: Verbatim: 'In traditional low-density (under 10 kW) facilities, loss of cooling ... meant that operators had several, sometimes tens of, minutes before inlet temperatures exceeded IT equipment tolerances' and 'IT systems using cold plates typically cannot tolerate loss of circulation for more than a few seconds (immersion tanks ride through several minutes).'
attrs.remedy: A density decision silently reclassifies the cooling plant as a UPS-backed critical load with generator-start-time constraints. Raise it in the electrical design review.
attrs.ground_contact: Fetched and quoted directly 2026-08-13.

nodes.label: Frontier rack power is forecast to surpass 200 kW as GPUs exceed 2 kW per module

attrs.missing_or_defect: Verbatim: rack power 'soon to surpass 200 kW' and 'as GPUs surpass 2 kW per module and CPUs approach 1 kW per socket'. This describes FRONTIER NEW BUILD, a different population from the modal installed base.
attrs.remedy: Use for shell and distribution headroom sizing, explicitly labelled as the frontier case, never as the expected mean.
attrs.ground_contact: Fetched and quoted directly 2026-08-13.

nodes.label: Coolant flow target is under 1.5 litres per kilowatt per minute at a 10 C rise

attrs.missing_or_defect: Verbatim: 'thermal engineering advances to keep flows under 1.5 liters per kilowatt per minute (at 10 C/18 F temperature rise)'. Independently derivable: water c_p = 4.186 kJ/kg.K, so 1 kW at 10 K rise needs 1/(4.186 x 10) = 0.0239 kg/s = 1.43 L/min per kW.
attrs.remedy: One of the very few density-coupling constants a learner can derive and check rather than memorise. Use it to size pipework from the compute roadmap.
attrs.ground_contact: Fetched and quoted directly 2026-08-13; first-principles check performed and agrees.

nodes.label: AI compute clusters can reach 150% of steady-state maximum power

attrs.missing_or_defect: Verbatim: 'AI compute clusters can sometimes reach 150% of their steady-state maximum power levels.'
attrs.remedy: Distribution sized on steady-state maxima is undersized by half for a synchronised cluster. Size branch circuits and UPS modules against the transient, not the average.
attrs.ground_contact: Fetched and quoted directly 2026-08-13.

nodes.label: Circuits and power systems are sized on the average of a diverse load population, not the combined peak

attrs.missing_or_defect: Verbatim: 'Many circuits and power systems are sized based on the average demand of a large and diverse population of IT loads, rather than their theoretical combined peak.' The VALIDITY CONDITION of the diversity factor is population diversity - which a single synchronised training cluster destroys.
attrs.remedy: Write the validity condition next to every diversity factor. A campus whose first tenant is one training job has a load population of size one and a factor of 1.0.
attrs.ground_contact: Fetched and quoted directly 2026-08-13.

nodes.label: Standard power telemetry samples at 100 ms and cannot see microsecond transients

attrs.missing_or_defect: Verbatim: 'Typical monitoring tools track GPU power every 100 milliseconds or more - too slow to detect the microsecond-speed spikes.'
attrs.remedy: The failure of the diversity assumption is not observable with taught instrumentation. Buy sub-100 ms power telemetry with phase one; retrofitting metering into an energised hall is expensive.
attrs.ground_contact: Fetched and quoted directly 2026-08-13.

nodes.label: Uptime's 2025 survey reports a 1.54 global average PUE among respondents
nodes.source_location: Google efficiency page, citing Uptime Institute 2025 Global Data Center Survey

attrs.missing_or_defect: Verbatim as quoted by Google: 'According to the Uptime Institute's 2025 Global Data Center Survey, the global average PUE of respondents' data centers was 1.54.' Read from Google's page, not from Uptime's survey directly.
attrs.remedy: Survey-of-respondents average, global, 2025. Not a design basis and not comparable to a modelled national stock average.
attrs.ground_contact: Read on Google's efficiency page 2026-08-13; the underlying Uptime survey was NOT opened - secondary attribution only.

nodes.label: Contractual utilisation floors are not taught as a capacity risk

attrs.missing_or_defect: The bank teaches stranded capacity as a physical mismatch. The largest and most durable stranding on a modern campus is contractual: an 85% minimum billing demand against a 50% national-average utilisation is 35 points of paid-for, undrawn capacity for a twelve-year term.
attrs.remedy: Add the contractual form of stranding to the syllabus and assess it by subtraction against a published tariff.
attrs.ground_contact: Both inputs read verbatim from primary sources 2026-08-13.

nodes.label: The density-to-ride-through coupling is not taught, so cooling is not reclassified as a critical load

attrs.missing_or_defect: Raising density from under 10 kW to cold-plate densities takes thermal ride-through from 'several, sometimes tens of, minutes' to 'a few seconds'. That is shorter than a diesel generator's start-and-transfer window, which reclassifies pumps and CDUs as UPS-backed critical loads. The coupling does not appear in the bank.
attrs.remedy: Teach ride-through as a function of density and make the electrical consequence explicit: a density decision rewrites the single-line diagram.
attrs.ground_contact: Uptime figures read directly 2026-08-13; the generator start-window comparison is this lineage's inference from L3's generator material.

nodes.label: The failure of the diversity assumption is invisible to the instrumentation the curriculum teaches

attrs.missing_or_defect: AI clusters reach 150% of steady-state maximum power in microsecond transients, while typical monitoring samples at 100 ms or slower. Operators discover the problem as a tripped breaker rather than as a metered trend. No item in the bank addresses telemetry sampling rate.
attrs.remedy: Teach sampling rate as a capacity-management parameter and specify sub-100 ms metering in phase-one scope.
attrs.ground_contact: Both Uptime figures read directly 2026-08-13; bank searched for telemetry sampling content with no matches.

nodes.label: A repeated vendor rack-power figure is circulation, not corroboration

attrs.remedy: Trace every rack-power figure to a primary vendor document or mark it unsourced. Two sources repeating an untraceable number is one rumour.
attrs.ground_contact: NVIDIA page and LBNL extrapolation statement both read directly 2026-08-13.

nodes.label: Density figures expire faster than the documents that quote them

nodes.label: Uptime Tier and TIA-942 Rated are not interchangeable, by Uptime's own statement

attrs.missing_or_defect: Verbatim: 'It is a common misconception in the data center industry that Tier Certification pertains to TIA-942. Furthermore, there is the misperception that these two standards are collaborative or synonymous.' And: 'we have not endorsed TIA-942 because it does not ensure the configuration and functionality necessary for high availability.'
