nodes.label: Month one: choose the heat rejection medium and economiser strategy before the site layout freezes

attrs.missing_or_defect: The nine-archetype menu (DX/CRAC, air-cooled chiller, water-cooled chiller, airside economiser, waterside economiser, dry cooler with/without adiabatic assist, airside economiser + adiabatic, and two liquid-cooled variants) is not a late mechanical detail: it sets yard area, pipe routes, structural loads, water demand, and the electrical load profile. Deferring it makes it a de-facto decision taken by whatever equipment is available.
attrs.remedy: Pick the archetype in month one against the site's wet-bulb record and the water/energy trade-off, and record the choice with its dated basis. Re-open only on a named trigger.
attrs.ground_contact: Grounded in the LBNL 2024 cooling-system taxonomy, which is the clearest open enumeration of the real decision menu.

nodes.label: Month one: set a numeric thermal ride-through budget and name how it is bought

attrs.missing_or_defect: Ride-through is treated as an emergent property of whatever plant gets built. It is not. It is purchased with four separable line items — UPS on air/coolant movers, room or loop volume, stored chilled water, and starting-point setpoint — each with a different cost and a different failure mode. If no one owns the number, no one buys any of them.
attrs.remedy: State the budget as: seconds of survivable cooling loss at design load, at the rack inlet, with the restart time of the heat-rejection plant subtracted. Then name which line item buys each second, and prove it at the integrated systems test.
attrs.ground_contact: Dell's measured ride-through curves plus Cundall's transient modelling both frame ride-through as a purchased quantity with identifiable levers.

nodes.label: Month one: fix the liquid-cooling loop boundary and who owns control authority at the CDU
nodes.source_location: Controls at the system level are typically provided by the facility...

attrs.missing_or_defect: Verbatim: 'Controls at the system level are typically provided by the facility, whereas controls at the node and component level are typically provided as part of the HPC system. It becomes less clear for levels in-between, such as the rack, CDU and branch. In these middle levels, provision for controls needs to be negotiated between the site and the supplier.' The CDU is exactly where the campus's resilience obligation and the IT vendor's thermal spec meet, and it is the layer with no default owner.
attrs.remedy: Write the boundary into the equipment RFP: who provides each measurement, at what cadence and accuracy, who may command flow and temperature, and what the facility BAS is allowed to see and do. Absent that clause the boundary is settled at commissioning, under schedule pressure.
attrs.ground_contact: Verbatim from the EE HPC WG liquid cooling controls whitepaper (LBNL-hosted, freely quotable).

nodes.label: Month one: select refrigerants against the 40 CFR 84.54 installation deadlines, not against catalogue availability

attrs.missing_or_defect: 40 CFR 84.54(c)(13) prohibits INSTALLING data centre / IT equipment facility / computer room cooling systems using a refrigerant of GWP 700 or greater, effective 2027-01-01; stand-alone chillers for comfort cooling are already restricted from 2025-01-01 under (a)(10)(i). A campus whose mechanical equipment is ordered against a pre-deadline catalogue and installed after the deadline has bought equipment it may not lawfully install.
attrs.remedy: Bind refrigerant GWP limits into the equipment specification at RFP, and check the installation date against the rule, not the order date. Carry the A2L consequences (flammability class, charge limits, leak detection, ventilation) into the room design at the same time.
attrs.ground_contact: Grounded verbatim in eCFR; the operational consequence is inferred.

nodes.label: 40 CFR 84.54 — HFC technology transitions restrictions (AIM Act)
nodes.source_location: § 84.54 Restrictions on the use of hydrofluorocarbons

attrs.missing_or_defect: Verbatim: '(a)(10)(i) Effective January 1, 2025, chillers for comfort cooling using a regulated substance, or a blend containing a regulated substance, with a global warming potential of 700 or greater'; '(a)(10)(iii) Effective January 1, 2026, chillers for industrial process refrigeration where the temperature of the fluid exiting the chiller is greater than -22 F (-30 C) ... with a global warming potential of 700 or greater'; '(a)(11) Effective January 1, 2027, self-contained products in data center, information technology equipment facility, and computer room cooling ... with a global warming potential of 700 or greater'; and the installation prohibition '(c)(13) Effective January 1, 2027, data center, information technology equipment facility, and computer room cooling systems using a regulated substance, or a blend containing a regulated substance, with a global warming potential of 700 or greater'. Paragraph (b) extends a sale/distribution ban three years after each (a) date.
attrs.remedy: Treat the (c)(13) date as an installation gate on the construction schedule, not as a procurement preference. Verify current text before relying on it — this part has been amended and reconsidered repeatedly.
attrs.ground_contact: EXTRACTED verbatim from the eCFR rendered text of § 84.54 on 2026-08-13.

nodes.label: Uptime Institute continuous cooling requirement (Accredited Tier Designer technical paper)

attrs.missing_or_defect: The publicly visible abstract states 'Tier IV is the only Tier that requires Continuous Cooling' and that the paper recommends continuous cooling 'at densities beyond 4 kilowatts (kW)/rack, regardless of Tier'. The 4 kW/rack recommendation threshold is roughly an order of magnitude below current AI rack densities, which means continuous cooling is effectively mandatory for the campus under discussion regardless of the Tier target.
attrs.remedy: Do not treat continuous cooling as a Tier IV luxury. Specify it, then define what it means numerically (see the ride-through budget decision) because the Tier Standard's own definition is behind the paywall and was not read.
attrs.ground_contact: Quoted from the public abstract page only; the Tier Standard: Topology document itself is paywalled and was NOT opened. No clause or section number is asserted.

nodes.label: Data-centre commissioning Levels 1-5 with Level 5 integrated systems test

attrs.missing_or_defect: Level 5, the integrated systems test or 'black building test', is described as the final gate before production IT load, run at design load with 'electrical load banks' pulling design kW and 'floor-standing heater load banks placed in the white space' dumping the same kW of heat the IT racks would. It is the only test in the sequence that can falsify a ride-through claim.
attrs.remedy: Make IST scope, load-bank heat provision, instrumentation time base, and pass/fail thresholds contractual at RFP stage. Heater load banks are frequently value-engineered out, which converts the IST into an electrical-only test that proves nothing thermal.
attrs.ground_contact: Read from a public field guide. The level definitions have no single open authority — see the ASHRAE Guideline 0 gap node.

nodes.label: Azure Australia East cooling outage, 2023-08-30
nodes.source_location: reporting on Microsoft's Post Incident Review

attrs.missing_or_defect: Utility voltage sag faulted five operating chillers simultaneously in an N+2 plant described as 'seven chillers, with five chillers in operation and two chillers in standby (N+2)'; only one of two standby units came up. Automatic restart failed because 'the corresponding pumps did not get the run signal from the chillers'. Manual restart then failed because 'the chilled water loop temperature had exceeded the threshold'. Recovery required shutting down servers, which 'successfully allowed the chilled water loop temperature to drop below the required threshold and enabled the restoration of the cooling capacity'. Night staffing was 'insufficient to restart the chillers in a timely manner' and was raised from three to seven.
attrs.remedy: This is the canonical shape of a cooling outage: redundant mechanical capacity present and healthy, defeated by a signalling dependency, then locked out by its own thermal state, then recovered only by shedding the load it existed to protect.
attrs.ground_contact: Passages attributed to Microsoft's PIR as reproduced by itnews.com.au; Microsoft's own status history page was not opened directly.

nodes.label: Google Cloud europe-west2-a cooling failure during the UK heatwave, 2022-07-19

attrs.missing_or_defect: Public incident text describes 'a cooling related failure in one of our buildings that hosts zone europe-west2-a for region europe-west2', beginning 2022-07-19 06:33 US/Pacific and resolved 2022-07-20 21:20. Impact included VM terminations and Persistent Disk failures. The status page references a fuller incident report that is not reproduced on the page.
attrs.remedy: Establishes that heat-rejection plant sized to a historical design wet bulb becomes a correlated failure across an entire building when the ambient exceeds it — the redundancy is N+1 against component failure, not against weather.
attrs.ground_contact: Read the Google Cloud Service Health incident page directly; the detailed root cause was NOT published on that page, so no mechanism is asserted here beyond 'cooling related failure'.

nodes.label: Oracle Cloud UK South cooling failure during the UK heatwave, 2022-07-19

attrs.missing_or_defect: Reported same-day, same-weather cooling failure in a second operator's London region, with Oracle reportedly stating that cooling units forced beyond their limits failed. Two independent operators failing on the same day on the same cause is a correlated regional exposure, not two coincidences.
attrs.remedy: Useful only as a correlation signal. Do not cite Oracle's wording from this node — the primary statement was not read.
attrs.ground_contact: UNGROUNDED — only search-result snippets were read; neither Oracle's incident statement nor the reporting pages were opened.

nodes.label: Central chilled water plant

attrs.missing_or_defect: A medium-temperature loop 'using a water supply temperature of 55F or higher improves chiller efficiency and eliminates uncontrolled phantom dehumidification loads', widens the waterside economiser window, and — critically for this lineage — provides a large water inventory that is the campus's principal thermal flywheel.
attrs.remedy: Specify the loop volume as a resilience parameter alongside the efficiency parameters. A plant optimised purely for low pumping energy and low pipe volume is a plant with less ride-through.
attrs.ground_contact: Grounded in the quoted source; see missing_or_defect for the extracted text.

nodes.label: Direct expansion computer room air conditioner (CRAC)

attrs.missing_or_defect: 'Direct expansion systems, typically called computer room air conditioners (CRACs), are commonly employed in small to midsize data centers because of their simplicity and cost-effectiveness. In these systems, refrigerant circulates directly through indoor coils to cool the data center air.' Refrigerant in the white space is what brings 40 CFR 84.54(c)(13) into scope for the room, not just the yard.
attrs.remedy: For a large campus, DX in the hall is mostly a legacy or edge choice; where it is used, the refrigerant deadline and the A2L consequences bind directly on the room.
attrs.ground_contact: Grounded in the quoted source; see missing_or_defect for the extracted text.

nodes.label: Computer room air handler (CRAH)

attrs.missing_or_defect: Distributed CRAH units versus a central air handler is a measurable efficiency fork — LBNL reports a facility on a central air handler using 'almost two-thirds of the input power to operate revenue-generating data center equipment, compared to the multiple small unit system that uses just over one-third'. Distributed units are also the population that fights itself on humidity.
attrs.remedy: Central, ducted, VSD air handling with shared sensors and setpoints; treat distributed units as a control-coordination liability, not just an efficiency one.
attrs.ground_contact: Grounded in the quoted source; see missing_or_defect for the extracted text.

nodes.label: Fan wall unit (FWU)

attrs.missing_or_defect: Fan wall units appear in the modelled chilled-water network alongside 'chillers, pumps, fan-wall units (FWUs), coolant distribution units (CDUs), and thermal stores'. Their relevance to this lineage is that they are an air-mover whose UPS backing status is a ride-through decision.
attrs.remedy: Decide explicitly whether FWUs are on UPS. Cundall found 'adding UPS support to distribution pumps and FWUs improved system response, delaying temperature increases and slightly reducing breach durations'.
attrs.ground_contact: Grounded in the quoted source; see missing_or_defect for the extracted text.

nodes.label: Air-side economiser

attrs.missing_or_defect: 'The cooling load for a data center is independent of the outdoor air temperature', so the economiser window is far wider than in an office. LBNL notes 'many data centers in cool climates use only economizer (air and/or water) cooling and no DX cooling', and that with MERV 13 filters 'the negative effects of outside air pollutants are small'. Requires a dewpoint lockout scheme where humidity is actively controlled, and is hard to retrofit because of duct size.
attrs.remedy: Decide at layout freeze — 'air-side economizers are not easy to add to an existing data center due to its large duct installations'. Locate intakes on the north side in the northern hemisphere.
attrs.ground_contact: Grounded in the quoted source; see missing_or_defect for the extracted text.

nodes.label: Water-side economiser

attrs.missing_or_defect: 'Free cooling is usually best suited for climates that have wet bulb temperatures lower than 55F for 3,000 or more hours per year' and 'most effectively serves chilled water loops designed for 50F and above'. Placing the heat exchanger upstream of the chillers rather than in parallel allows partial free cooling — 'the chillers operate at reduced load to meet the chilled water supply set point'.
attrs.remedy: Site the heat exchanger upstream, not in parallel; the piping decision is not reversible later and it determines whether partial-hours free cooling is available at all.
attrs.ground_contact: Grounded in the quoted source; see missing_or_defect for the extracted text.

nodes.label: Dry cooler with adiabatic assist

attrs.missing_or_defect: 'When the outdoor dry bulb temperature is low, the dry coolers efficiently reject heat using ambient air alone. With adiabatic assistance, spraying or circulating water through pads upstream of the heat exchanger coils enhances cooling, especially when the dry bulb temperature is high and the wet bulb temperature is low... This system conserves water compared to evaporative cooling towers.' LBNL also finds these 'exhibit the highest water consumption among the remaining scenarios' when wet mode activates.
attrs.remedy: Adiabatic assist is a water/energy dial, not a water-free option. Size the wet-mode hours from the site's dry-bulb/wet-bulb record and carry them into the water budget.
attrs.ground_contact: Grounded in the quoted source; see missing_or_defect for the extracted text.

nodes.label: Evaporative cooling tower

attrs.missing_or_defect: Oversized towers with VFD fans give 'a smaller approach to ambient wet bulb temperature, thus allowing for operation at lower cold condenser water temperatures'; LBNL recommends 'a 5F to 7F approach cooling tower plant with a condenser water temperature reset'. Open towers bring an obligatory water management program for microbial control.
attrs.remedy: Specify approach and turndown, and stand up the water management program as a commissioning deliverable rather than an operations afterthought.
attrs.ground_contact: Grounded in the quoted source; see missing_or_defect for the extracted text.

nodes.label: Hot aisle / cold aisle containment

attrs.missing_or_defect: 'With proper isolation, the temperature of the hot aisle no longer impacts the temperature of the racks... the hot aisle becomes a heat exhaust.' Containment raises return temperature (often '85F or higher', and 'rack return air temperatures can exceed 100F when densely populated'), which is what makes economiser hours and higher chilled water temperatures available at all.
attrs.remedy: Containment is upstream of the economiser business case, not parallel to it. Also treat it as a ride-through device — see the containment/ride-through finding.
attrs.ground_contact: Grounded in the quoted source; see missing_or_defect for the extracted text.

nodes.label: Rack blanking panels and rack-gap sealing

attrs.missing_or_defect: 'Any opening will degrade the separation of hot and cold air'. The DOE deck records a measured case where 'one 12" blanking panel reduced temperature ~20F'. Recirculation causes listed are 'too little supply airflow, lack of blanking panels, gaps between racks, short equipment rows'.
attrs.remedy: Blanking is the cheapest thermal intervention in the building and the one most reliably lost during churn. Make blanking-panel state an audited asset, not a build-time task.
attrs.ground_contact: Grounded in the quoted source; see missing_or_defect for the extracted text.

nodes.label: Chimney / ducted-rack containment

attrs.missing_or_defect: Dell reports that 'tight containment like a chimney product' with 'a sealed front door enclosing a deep front plenum' lengthened the distance from IT exhaust to intake and 'helps to dampen the extreme temperatures that the IT systems see during the cooling outage'.
attrs.remedy: Where UPS on air handlers is not affordable, tight containment is the substitute lever for ride-through — Dell states 'the dampening may be enough to lessen the risk for facilities not leveraging a UPS'.
attrs.ground_contact: Grounded in the quoted source; see missing_or_defect for the extracted text.

nodes.label: Rear-door heat exchanger

attrs.missing_or_defect: A 'localized air-to-liquid heat exchanger (coil) placed at the back of a server-rack that captures server heat'. Passive variants use server fans; active variants add fans. It is the liquid-cooling option that leaves the server untouched and therefore the one that can be retrofitted into an air-cooled hall.
attrs.remedy: Use as the bridge technology for mixed halls; note it still consumes facility water temperature and CDU capacity, so it competes with direct-to-chip for the same loop.
attrs.ground_contact: Grounded in the quoted source; see missing_or_defect for the extracted text.

nodes.label: Direct-to-chip cold plate cooling (single-phase)

attrs.missing_or_defect: 'Standard fin-based heat sinks on chips are replaced with cold plates that have liquid flowing through channels to remove heat (solution generally involves a CDU).' Schneider states '60% to 90% of a liquid-cooled server's heat can be removed via the liquid, depending on the number of liquid-cooled components. The remaining heat is removed by air cooling.'
attrs.remedy: Do not delete the air plant. A 60-90% liquid capture fraction means the hall still needs a sized, redundant air system for the residual, and that residual is what fails first.
attrs.ground_contact: Grounded in the quoted source; see missing_or_defect for the extracted text.

nodes.label: Two-phase direct-to-chip cooling

attrs.missing_or_defect: Distinguished in the CDU taxonomy as refrigerant-to-air (R-A), where the 'two-phase direct-to-chip system rejects heat directly to air via a radiator... like an air-based condenser', and refrigerant-to-liquid (R-L), which 'operates like a water-based condenser'.
attrs.remedy: If two-phase is on the table, the refrigerant GWP rule and the leak/charge regime follow it into the white space — the same exposure as DX, at rack scale.
attrs.ground_contact: Grounded in the quoted source; see missing_or_defect for the extracted text.

nodes.label: Single-phase immersion cooling

attrs.missing_or_defect: 'Single-phase immersion cooling, in which heat load is transferred to dielectric oil/fluid that is pumped around electronics by a CDU.' Schneider notes 'immersion tanks also have flow requirements of the dielectric across the servers' and that floor-mounted CDUs 'for immersion systems can be integrated into the tanks'.
attrs.remedy: Immersion changes the service model (fluid handling, drip, hoisting) more than it changes the thermal model. Budget the operations change, not just the capital.
attrs.ground_contact: Grounded in the quoted source; see missing_or_defect for the extracted text.

nodes.label: Two-phase immersion cooling

attrs.missing_or_defect: 'Two-phase immersion, in which an engineered dielectric fluid with a boiling point below IT components' maximum operating temperatures removes heat load by undergoing a liquid-to-gas phase change, with that vapor transferring heat to a vapor-to-liquid heat exchanger, which then condenses back to a liquid in a passive cycle.'
attrs.remedy: The passive condensing cycle is the only white-space cooling mechanism in this list that does not require a pump or fan to keep working in the first seconds of a power loss — that is a ride-through property worth quantifying, and it is not quantified anywhere I could reach.
attrs.ground_contact: Grounded in the quoted source; see missing_or_defect for the extracted text.

nodes.label: Coolant distribution unit (CDU)
nodes.source_location: Describing liquid cooling architectures; 2. CDU type

attrs.missing_or_defect: The CDU isolates the IT fluid loop from the rest of the cooling system and performs five functions: 'temperature control, flow control, pressure control, fluid treatment, heat exchange and isolation'. Capacities: rack-mounted 20-40 kW (liquid-to-air) or 40-80 kW (liquid-to-liquid); floor-mounted liquid-to-air 'up to about 60 kW'; floor-mounted liquid-to-liquid '300 kW to greater than 1 MW'. Schneider is explicit that facility water 'cannot run directly through a chip's cold plate. Doing so can corrode metals and tiny fluid channels within the cold plate.'
attrs.remedy: The CDU is the campus's new single point of thermal aggregation. Treat each CDU as a named failure domain in the cut-set model with its own redundancy, ride-through and control-authority answer.
attrs.ground_contact: Grounded in the quoted source; see missing_or_defect for the extracted text.

nodes.label: Negative-pressure (sub-atmospheric) CDU with leak prevention system

attrs.missing_or_defect: 'TCSs are commonly operated under a positive pressure, but alternative CDUs can pump water under a vacuum, or often called negative pressure, eliminating the risk of leaks in the TCS. This feature is commonly called a leak-prevention-system (LPS).' Schneider also claims it simplifies connections and components 'which can reduce the overall cost'.
attrs.remedy: Where liquid enters the white space above live electrical equipment, negative pressure converts the worst failure mode from an expulsion into an ingress. Evaluate it explicitly rather than defaulting to positive pressure.
attrs.ground_contact: Grounded in the quoted source; see missing_or_defect for the extracted text.

nodes.label: Side-stream filtration and coolant chemistry treatment

attrs.missing_or_defect: Trade guidance frames the risk as 'scaling can insulate heat exchanger surfaces, corrosion can damage equipment and microbial growth can lead to biofouling', and states that for closed systems 'the margin for error is even more narrow'. Recommended equipment includes side-stream filtration, chemical dosing and 'sensor-based control technologies, including chemical tagging and real-time diagnostics'.
attrs.remedy: Specify treatment, filtration and monitoring as a system with an owner and a sampling cadence at RFP, because the numeric limits it must hit are behind the ASHRAE gap and must be supplied by the IT vendor's own coolant specification.
attrs.ground_contact: Grounded in the quoted source; see missing_or_defect for the extracted text.

nodes.label: Chilled water thermal energy storage tank
nodes.source_location: Understanding thermal resilience is key during an outage

attrs.missing_or_defect: 'During a mains power failure, the thermal store provides a temporary reserve of chilled water while chillers are offline or restarting. That stored thermal energy slows the rate of increase in the system's supply temperature.' Cundall found 'the most significant improvement came from the introduction of thermal storage', ahead of UPS on pumps and FWUs. LBNL separately notes a storage tank 'can also be an economical alternative to additional mechanical cooling capacity' and 'provides the additional benefit of backup make-up water for cooling towers'.
attrs.remedy: Size the tank from the transient model against the measured restart time of the actual chillers specified, not from a rule of thumb in minutes.
attrs.ground_contact: Grounded in the quoted source; see missing_or_defect for the extracted text.

nodes.label: UPS-backed cooling pumps and air movers

attrs.missing_or_defect: Dell: 'The addition of UPS support to data center air handlers turns seconds of ride-through time into minutes' and 'the incremental cost to add UPS capability to cover the facility fans should be no more than an additional 5%-15% above what you are spending to back up the IT.' Cundall found UPS on distribution pumps and FWUs 'improved system response, delaying temperature increases and slightly reducing breach durations'.
attrs.remedy: Put air and coolant movers on the UPS as the default and force anyone removing them to state the ride-through seconds they are deleting.
attrs.ground_contact: Grounded in the quoted source; see missing_or_defect for the extracted text.

nodes.label: Uninterruptible power supply

attrs.missing_or_defect: In this lineage the UPS is not an IT-load device: it is the mechanism that keeps coolant and air moving through the gap between utility loss and heat-rejection restart. LBNL's own framing is IT-centric ('evaluate which equipment, if not the entire data center, requires a UPS system'), which is exactly the framing that leaves pumps and fans off the protected bus.
attrs.remedy: Size the UPS to the mechanical ride-through requirement as well as the IT requirement, and make the mechanical share a named line in the load schedule so it cannot be quietly trimmed.
attrs.ground_contact: Grounded in the quoted source; see missing_or_defect for the extracted text.

nodes.label: Transient (second-by-second) thermal model of the cooling network
nodes.source_location: Why is transient analysis becoming more important?

attrs.missing_or_defect: 'Traditional cooling calculations are typically based on stable operating conditions.' A transient model instead simulates 'second-by-second behaviour in failure scenarios'. Cundall modelled 'the entire chilled-water network... chillers, pumps, fan-wall units (FWUs), coolant distribution units (CDUs), and thermal stores' and validated against a live Level 4 test to 'within 0.2C'.
attrs.remedy: Make a validated transient model a contract deliverable at design stage and re-validate it against the IST. It converts ride-through from an argument into a checkable number.
attrs.ground_contact: Grounded in the quoted source; see missing_or_defect for the extracted text.

nodes.label: Level 5 integrated systems test with heater load banks
nodes.source_location: load bank configuration; thermal ride-through verification

attrs.missing_or_defect: 'Load banks stand in for the IT load, and the test runs at the design load the plant was built to carry, not at no-load', with 'floor-standing heater load banks placed in the white space dump the same kW of heat the IT racks would'. The test instruments 'the bus, the transfers, and the chilled water and rack inlet temps on a time base fast enough to catch the transient', capturing 'peak rack inlet temperature' and 'recovery time'.
attrs.remedy: Electrical-only ISTs are common because heater load banks cost money and floor space. An electrical-only IST cannot falsify a thermal ride-through claim and must not be accepted as proof of one.
attrs.ground_contact: Grounded in the quoted source; see missing_or_defect for the extracted text.

nodes.label: Building management system / building automation system

attrs.missing_or_defect: The BMS/BAS is where the cooling plant's sequences, interlocks and permissives live. The EE HPC WG table fixes the measurement contract it needs: water flow +/-5% every 30 s, thermal data +/-1 C every 60 s at system level and +/-2 C once per second at node/component, pump speed +/-3%, pressure differential +/-10 kPa every 5 s, valve position +/-5% every 60 s at system level and +/-2% every 3 s at rack level.
attrs.remedy: Specify the measurement contract (point, provider, cadence, accuracy) in the BMS scope. A sequence that is correct but blind at 60-second granularity cannot manage a transient that completes in seconds.
attrs.ground_contact: Grounded in the quoted source; see missing_or_defect for the extracted text.

_provenance: L9 lineage synthesis across the sources listed in l9-operations.md

nodes.label: Rack inlet temperature sensing from onboard server sensors
nodes.source_location: 4.2 Aisle Separation and Containment (thermal best practices)

attrs.missing_or_defect: 'Control supply temperature (and airflow) based on IT equipment intake air temperatures and not on the return temperature. Use wired or wireless external-to-rack temperature sensors or, even better, network data exchange with IT equipment on-board temperature sensors. All ENERGY STAR servers have the latter capability.'
attrs.remedy: Return-air control is the single most common sensing defect and it is the one that makes a starved rack invisible to the plant. Wire intake sensing, and prefer the servers' own sensors.
attrs.ground_contact: Grounded in the quoted source; see missing_or_defect for the extracted text.

nodes.label: CFD airflow model of the white space
nodes.source_location: When to implement (reject heat to air in IT space)

attrs.missing_or_defect: Schneider gates the closed-loop liquid-to-air architecture on 'sufficient air-cooled capacity and airflow analysis or computational fluid dynamics (CFD) indicates the room can support the high densities' — i.e. CFD is the instrument that tests whether aggregate capacity is actually deliverable at the rack.
attrs.remedy: Require CFD (or measured airflow analysis) as the acceptance evidence for any high-density deployment into an existing air-cooled hall, and re-run it after layout churn.
attrs.ground_contact: Grounded in the quoted source; see missing_or_defect for the extracted text.

nodes.label: Rack Cooling Index (RCI)
nodes.source_location: 4 Air Management; DOE Air Management Tool

attrs.missing_or_defect: LBNL states the intake temperature data 'can be made actionable by using the Rack Cooling Index (RCI)' and that 'the Department of Energy's Air Management Tool uses the RCI for that purpose'. It is the available open metric for compliance of intake temperatures across a population of racks rather than at an average.
attrs.remedy: Adopt RCI as the reporting metric for air management, but note it is parameterised by the recommended/allowable envelope, which is the ASHRAE gap — so the metric cannot be evaluated until a human supplies those limits.
attrs.ground_contact: Grounded in the quoted source; see missing_or_defect for the extracted text.

nodes.label: Leak detection and containment for white-space liquid loops

attrs.missing_or_defect: Leak risk is managed structurally, not only by sensing: negative-pressure CDUs are described as 'eliminating the risk of leaks in the TCS', and rack-mounted CDUs are credited with 'limits potential failure modes to a single rack (e.g., TCS leak or contamination)'.
attrs.remedy: Decide leak strategy at architecture time (loop pressure regime and loop blast radius), then add detection. Detection added to a positive-pressure, whole-row loop is the weakest of the three options.
attrs.ground_contact: Grounded in the quoted source; see missing_or_defect for the extracted text.

nodes.label: Ride-through time is a purchased quantity with four separable levers, not a property of the plant

attrs.missing_or_defect: Dell enumerates the variables as room density, 'operating temperature (at the start of failure)', 'amount of facility air over-provisioning relative to IT air consumption', 'room height', 'facility air and coolant movers (fans or pumps) with or without UPS back up', 'some containment systems', and 'IT power density'. Each is a separate purchase order. A design that never states a ride-through target buys none of them deliberately.
attrs.remedy: Put ride-through seconds into the basis of design as a numeric requirement with an owner, traceable to the four levers.
attrs.ground_contact: EXTRACTED from Dell's white paper, which reports instrumented tests in an 876 sq ft lab.

nodes.label: The rack-inlet temperature curve after cooling loss has two regimes with different physics

attrs.missing_or_defect: 'When the cool air production stops, there is a short period during which racks still have access to the cold air... The initial steep ramp depicts the period of consumption of this cool air.' Then 'the period to the right of the inflection point shows the IT equipment heating up the air and equipment within the room — the room no longer has the ability to remove its own heat.' Regime one is set by aisle air inventory; regime two is set by room volume and density.
attrs.remedy: Design interventions must be matched to the regime: over-provisioning air only flattens the first ramp, room height and thermal storage flatten the second, and UPS on air movers changes which regime you are in at all.
attrs.ground_contact: EXTRACTED verbatim from Dell's measured curves.

nodes.label: UPS on the air movers converts seconds of ride-through into minutes, for 5-15% above the IT UPS cost

attrs.missing_or_defect: 'If you are deployed with this level of density, it is only a matter of seconds until you are over spec in the still data center, but if the air is moving, this extends your time to minutes.' Cost: 'no more than an additional 5%-15% above what you are spending to back up the IT.' Dell's 350 W/sq ft test without UPS on the air handlers reached '50C to 60C (122F to 140F)' rack inlet, at which 'over-temperature protection limits built into all power supplies... would likely trigger'.
attrs.remedy: Default to UPS-backed air and coolant movers. This is the highest-yield, lowest-cost ride-through purchase in the whole mechanical scope.
attrs.ground_contact: EXTRACTED from Dell's instrumented 350 W/sq ft test.

nodes.label: Room height roughly scales ride-through; lowering the setpoint buys seconds, not minutes
nodes.source_location: Room Height; Lower Normal Operating Temperature

attrs.missing_or_defect: 'If the room height is doubled, it should approximately double the ride-through time.' By contrast, 'the effect on ride-through time of the temperature set point is linear. If starting 5C (9F) lower, you will be about 5C lower at all times during a failure'; a 12-degree colder start 'will still only buy you seconds on the non-UPS trajectory' while 'you will be incurring a continuous OpEx penalty'.
attrs.remedy: Never run the hall cold as a resilience strategy. It is the most expensive second of ride-through available and it is bought every hour of the year.
attrs.ground_contact: EXTRACTED from Dell; the test room volume is stated as 11,400 cubic feet above the raised floor and 1,314 cubic feet below, at 876 square feet.

nodes.label: Air over-provisioning changes the initial rise but does not extend ride-through
nodes.source_location: Figure 3; Inlet Temperatures of Different Racks

attrs.missing_or_defect: 'It appears that volumetric over-provisioning of Rack B's aisle did not lengthen overall ride-through time, since the rack that was initially cooler (Rack B) caught up to the hotter rack (Rack A) within a fairly short time frame.' Excess airflow buys a better steady state, not a longer survival window.
attrs.remedy: Do not credit airflow over-provisioning against a ride-through requirement. It is an air management improvement being counted twice.
attrs.ground_contact: EXTRACTED from Dell's two-rack comparison at 450 W/sq ft.

nodes.label: Liquid cooling raises heat load per unit of coolant inventory, so the ride-through problem gets harder as density rises
nodes.source_location: Introduction; Why is transient analysis becoming more important?

attrs.missing_or_defect: 'Compared with traditional air-cooled facilities, liquid-cooled systems must handle far greater heat loads, so they tend to have lower thermal inertia, posing an additional challenge.' And: 'Liquid cooling systems tend to operate within tighter thermal boundaries. This means that even relatively short temperature increases can become significant to operation... In high-density data centres, this happens in a matter of seconds.'
attrs.remedy: The intuition that liquid holds more heat than air is wrong at the system level once the load scales with it. Model the transient rather than reasoning from heat capacity.
attrs.ground_contact: EXTRACTED from a UK engineering consultancy blog dated 2026-07-01 describing its own modelling and a validated live test.

nodes.label: Small technology-cooling loops have short ride-through; the loop that limits blast radius is the loop that dies fastest
nodes.source_location: Reject heat to air in IT space — Disadvantages; floor-mounted advantages

attrs.missing_or_defect: Schneider lists as a disadvantage of the rack-level liquid-to-air architecture: 'Small water based TCS loops have short thermal ride through, which means if the CDU fans fail, the volume of water in the loop won't have much cooling capacity to support the load compared to other architectures.' And for floor-mounted CDUs: 'More thermal ride thru than rack-mounted CDUs', but 'All racks on single TCS loop become susceptible to common cause failures (e.g., TCS leaks, contamination, controls, etc.)'.
attrs.remedy: This is a genuine, unavoidable trade: loop volume buys time, loop scope buys blast radius. Decide it against the workload — Schneider's own gate is whether the workload 'can tolerate a common cause failure (e.g., loss of fluid flow) for all racks served by a single CDU'.
attrs.ground_contact: EXTRACTED verbatim from Schneider Electric White Paper 133 v2.

nodes.label: In a modelled total utility loss, thermal storage outperformed UPS on pumps and fan walls
nodes.source_location: Understanding thermal resilience is key during an outage

attrs.missing_or_defect: 'Adding UPS support to distribution pumps and FWUs improved system response, delaying temperature increases and slightly reducing breach durations. However, the most significant improvement came from the introduction of thermal storage.' Without buffering, in one modelled high-density scenario, temperature thresholds were breached within seconds.
attrs.remedy: Do not treat UPS-on-pumps and thermal storage as alternatives — the modelling ranks storage first for chilled-water systems, while Dell's air-side testing ranks UPS-on-fans first. The two results are about different plant, not in conflict.
attrs.ground_contact: EXTRACTED from Cundall's description of its own modelling; the underlying model and inputs are proprietary and were not seen.

nodes.label: The binding constraint is heat-rejection restart time, and restart can be blocked by the thermal state the outage created

attrs.missing_or_defect: 'We have seen the risks of this in Sydney, where such high return water temperatures can make it difficult to restart chillers after a failure. By the time the chillers restart, the water temperature is so high that it can cause overpressure in the evaporators, causing the chillers to shut down again even after a few minutes.' The IST field guide gives a typical chiller restart window of '4 to 5 minutes' during which 'thermal energy storage must cover the gap'.
attrs.remedy: Ride-through must be specified as: survivable seconds MINUS the measured restart time of the specified machines, including the possibility of a failed first start. A plant that rides through for four minutes and restarts in five has zero margin.
attrs.ground_contact: EXTRACTED from two independent sources — a consultancy blog and a commissioning field guide.

nodes.label: Hot-loop restart lockout is a self-reinforcing failure: the outage creates the condition that prevents recovery

attrs.missing_or_defect: In Azure Australia East, manual restart attempts failed because 'the chilled water loop temperature had exceeded the threshold'. Recovery required shutting down servers, which 'successfully allowed the chilled water loop temperature to drop below the required threshold and enabled the restoration of the cooling capacity'. The same mechanism is described independently for Sydney by Cundall as evaporator overpressure on restart.
attrs.remedy: Design and rehearse the load-shed path as part of the cooling recovery sequence, and know the loop temperature threshold that locks out the chillers. If the only exit from the lockout is shedding IT load, that is the recovery plan whether or not anyone wrote it down.
attrs.ground_contact: Two independent descriptions of the same mechanism (an operator PIR as reported, and an engineering consultancy's field experience). Note the Uptime-style aggregate statistics behind this pattern are paywalled and were not read.

nodes.label: When ride-through is exhausted, the recovery action is to shed IT load — so IT load shedding is a mechanical control

attrs.missing_or_defect: Azure shut down servers to let the chilled water loop cool. The EE HPC WG procurement questions ask the owner directly: 'During high wet bulb periods and/or low available chiller capacity, is load shedding/processor throttling an option?' and 'Will load or demand limiting or load shedding be utilized? In what circumstances will this be done?'
attrs.remedy: Write the thermal load-shed policy before the building opens: which workloads, in what order, on whose authority, at what measured trigger. Doing this during the incident is how an outage becomes an eight-hour outage.
attrs.ground_contact: EXTRACTED: the incident behaviour from the PIR reporting, the design question verbatim from the EE HPC WG whitepaper.

nodes.label: IT shutdown thresholds are vendor-specific and sit well above the allowable inlet limit — the cliff is not where the spec is

attrs.missing_or_defect: Dell states 'most IT systems have an operating maximum temperature of around 35C (95F)' but that 'Dell systems typically will not hit a shutdown trigger point until at least 10C (18F) past the maximum allowable temperature', that 'by design, Dell does not force a shutdown at high temperatures', that power supply over-temperature protection 'would likely trigger by the time inlet temperatures reach the 50C-60C levels', and that 'other vendors may have default shutdown limits that are lower than this'. Short excursions 'will have no measurable effect on long-term reliability'.
attrs.remedy: Obtain the shutdown and throttle thresholds per IT platform in writing and use the LOWEST one in the fleet as the ride-through pass criterion. Do not use the environmental envelope limit as the shutdown limit — they are different numbers with different consequences.
attrs.ground_contact: EXTRACTED from Dell (vendor statements about its own equipment). NO ASHRAE class values are asserted here; the environmental envelope authority remains UNGROUNDED by design.

nodes.label: Chilled water valve state at the instant of power loss changes the recovery transient, and blower control chases the valve
nodes.source_location: Appendix A: Temperature Bounce after Generator Start

attrs.missing_or_defect: 'In our test scenario, the CRAH units were shut down in standard fashion, which caused the chilled water valves to slowly reduce flow down to completely closed. With a power failure, however, they would be stuck open without backup.' On re-energisation 'the CRAH unit blowers ramp quickly to 100% flow... After reaching 100%, they look to their control algorithm. By default, they seek the same percentage of maximum speed as the chilled water valve is open... the temperature climbs back up as the flow rate goes down.'
attrs.remedy: Interrogate the actual fail position of every control valve and damper, and interrogate the post-restoration control sequence separately. A correct steady-state sequence can produce a second temperature excursion after power returns.
attrs.ground_contact: EXTRACTED verbatim from Dell's test anomaly appendix — one of the few open, instrumented descriptions of a mechanical control sequence misbehaving during recovery.

nodes.label: Bypass and recirculation are distinct defects with distinct causes and opposite symptoms

attrs.missing_or_defect: Bypass air 'wastes fan energy as well as cooling energy and capacity'; recirculation 'increases inlet temperature to servers'. Bypass causes: 'too much supply airflow, misplaced perforated tiles, leaky cable penetrations, too-high tile exit velocity'. Recirculation causes: 'too little supply airflow, lack of blanking panels, gaps between racks, short equipment rows'. The two defects coexist in the same room and the fix for one can worsen the other.
attrs.remedy: Diagnose per aisle, not per room. Increasing supply airflow to fix a recirculating aisle manufactures bypass elsewhere and hides the original defect behind higher fan power.
attrs.ground_contact: EXTRACTED verbatim from the DOE/FEMP air management training deck.

nodes.label: Aggregate cooling capacity can be sufficient while individual racks starve — airflow distribution is not fungible
nodes.source_location: 4.3 Optimize Supply and Return Air Configuration

attrs.missing_or_defect: LBNL names the precise mechanism: 'high air velocity in the under-floor plenum... can create localized negative static pressure and draw room air back into the under-floor plenum. Equipment closer to downflow CRAC units or computer room air handlers (CRAH) can receive too little cooling air due to this effect.' The racks that starve are the ones NEAREST the cooling units — the opposite of the intuition that proximity means capacity.
attrs.remedy: Capacity accounting in kW or tons is not a cooling model. Only a pressure/flow model (CFD or measured) can tell you whether a given rack is fed. Deeper plenums and CRAH placement are the design-time controls.
attrs.ground_contact: EXTRACTED verbatim from the LBNL/DOE Best Practices Guide, July 2025 edition.

nodes.label: Cable congestion in the plenum reduces total airflow AND degrades its distribution

attrs.missing_or_defect: 'Cable congestion in raised-floor plenums can sharply reduce the total airflow as well as degrade the airflow distribution through the perforated floor tiles. Both effects promote the development of hot spots.' LBNL specifies 'a minimum effective (clear) height of 24 inches... for raised-floor installations' and recommends 'a cable mining program (i.e., a program to remove abandoned or inoperable cables)'.
attrs.remedy: Plenum clear height and a standing cable-mining program are thermal controls, not cable hygiene. Abandoned cable is a slow, invisible derate of the cooling system.
attrs.ground_contact: EXTRACTED verbatim from the LBNL/DOE Best Practices Guide.

nodes.label: Moving floor tiles to fix a hot spot is a global change made with local intent
nodes.source_location: 4.3 Optimize Supply and Return Air Configuration

attrs.missing_or_defect: 'The location of supply tiles needs to be carefully considered to prevent short circuiting of supply air and checked periodically if users are likely to reconfigure them. Removing or adding tiles to fix hot spots can cause problems throughout the system.' The DOE deck adds the operational rule: 'Place perforated floor tiles only in cold aisles' and 'rebalance with new IT or HVAC equipment'.
attrs.remedy: Put tile layout under change control with the same seriousness as a patch panel. Every unrecorded tile move is an undocumented modification to the cooling system.
attrs.ground_contact: EXTRACTED verbatim from two DOE/LBNL sources.

nodes.label: Containment is a ride-through device, not only an efficiency device

attrs.missing_or_defect: Dell's containment case 'helps to dampen the extreme temperatures that the IT systems see during the cooling outage' because 'the distance from IT exhaust to intake is quite lengthened', and states 'the dampening may be enough to lessen the risk for facilities not leveraging a UPS'. Containment is almost universally justified on PUE, so its resilience contribution is invisible in the business case and therefore first to be value-engineered.
attrs.remedy: Include containment in the ride-through model, and require the transient model to be re-run if containment scope changes during value engineering.
attrs.ground_contact: EXTRACTED from Dell's instrumented containment test at 350 W/sq ft.

nodes.label: Containment degrades continuously under operations: leakage gaps, churn, and manual intervention during heat events

attrs.missing_or_defect: The LBNL/NERSC operating experience states the hot-aisle separation panel system 'works, but' — 'potentially requires manual control adjustments during heat storms', 'important to seal leakage gaps in separation panels and racks', and 'containments are difficult to balance with IT equipment maintenance & reconfigurations'. It adds that 'BMS automation has proved to be difficult and expensive' and 'keeping the system running requires considerable admin attention'.
attrs.remedy: Budget recurring labour for containment integrity and put leakage inspection on a schedule. Containment installed and never re-inspected converges toward no containment.
attrs.ground_contact: EXTRACTED verbatim from an operator's own lessons slide in the DOE/FEMP deck.

nodes.label: Containment is upstream of the economiser hours, which are upstream of the whole water/energy trade
nodes.source_location: 4.4 Other Benefits of Raising Temperature Set Points

attrs.missing_or_defect: 'As the return air temperature is increased through the use of good air management... the temperature at which an air-side economizer will save energy is correspondingly increased. Designing for a higher return air temperature increases the number of hours that outside air, or a waterside economizer/free cooling, can be used.' Server air temperature rise is stated as '10F to more than 40F', with rack return 'exceed[ing] 100F when densely populated'.
attrs.remedy: Sequence the design: containment first, then setpoints, then chilled water temperature, then economiser sizing. Sizing the economiser before fixing air management sizes it for a room that will not exist.
attrs.ground_contact: EXTRACTED verbatim from the LBNL/DOE Best Practices Guide.

nodes.label: In the public record, cooling outages are signalling and sequencing failures, not capacity failures

attrs.missing_or_defect: Azure Australia East: chillers faulted on a voltage sag and would not auto-restart because 'the corresponding pumps did not get the run signal from the chillers' — the pumps and chillers were both functional. Google europe-west4-a (2026): 'the chiller controller dropped offline during the voltage transient event, failing to signal the chilled water distribution pumps to restart' — again, the chillers themselves did not fail. In both cases redundant mechanical capacity was present, healthy, and unreachable.
attrs.remedy: Model controllers, permissives, run signals and their power sources as first-class nodes in the cut-set model. Mechanical redundancy counted without its control path is redundancy that has not been counted.
attrs.ground_contact: Two operator-published incident accounts (one direct from Google Cloud Service Health via the L3 lineage, one via press reporting of Microsoft's PIR). This is convergent evidence from independent operators, not circulation of a single claim.

nodes.label: Controls fail on the same transient that creates the demand for them

attrs.missing_or_defect: The Google europe-west4-a report states the chiller controller 'dropped offline during the voltage transient event'. Azure Australia East's five chillers faulted on the same power sag. In both cases the disturbance that made cooling recovery necessary is the disturbance that disabled the mechanism for recovering it — a textbook common-cause dependency crossing the electrical/mechanical boundary.
attrs.remedy: Ride-through the control plane explicitly: controllers, VFDs, actuators, BMS field controllers and the network between them belong on protected power and in the transient test, not just the pumps and fans they command.
attrs.ground_contact: Quoted from the Google Cloud incident report as captured in wave 1's L3 fragment plus the Azure PIR reporting.

nodes.label: A cooling control system sampling at 30-60 seconds cannot manage an event that completes in seconds
nodes.source_location: TABLE: DATA INPUTS FOR DYNAMIC CONTROLS

attrs.missing_or_defect: The EE HPC WG table sets facility-level water flow at 'once every 30 sec', thermal data at 'once every 60 sec', valve position at 'once per 60 sec', pressure differential at 'once per 5 sec', with node and component thermal data at 'once per sec'. Against Cundall's finding that high-density thermal excursions occur 'in a matter of seconds', the facility-side cadence is one to two orders of magnitude too slow to see the event it must survive.
attrs.remedy: Separate the efficiency control loop from the protection loop. Efficiency can sample at 60 s; protection interlocks and the IST instrumentation need a fast time base — the IST field guide requires 'a time base fast enough to catch the transient'.
attrs.ground_contact: EXTRACTED from the EE HPC WG table (LBNL-hosted); the mismatch conclusion is inferred by comparison with the Cundall and IST sources.

nodes.label: The control-authority boundary at the CDU, rack and branch has no default owner

attrs.missing_or_defect: Verbatim: 'It becomes less clear for levels in-between, such as the rack, CDU and branch. In these middle levels, provision for controls needs to be negotiated between the site and the supplier of the HPC system.' The whitepaper's own procurement questions include 'Will an interface be available to the facility's control system? What information will be made available? What communications protocols and connections will be used?' — questions that only get asked if someone remembers to ask them.
attrs.remedy: Make the control interface an RFP line item with named points, protocol, cadence, accuracy and command authority. This is the single cheapest intervention in the entire liquid-cooling scope and it expires the moment the equipment is ordered.
attrs.ground_contact: EXTRACTED verbatim from the EE HPC WG liquid cooling controls whitepaper.

nodes.label: The IT vendor's allowable flow and temperature excursion magnitude and duration is the term that makes ride-through checkable

attrs.missing_or_defect: The whitepaper's vendor questions include: 'What are the allowable flow and temperature excursion magnitudes and durations?', 'Does the system have internal thermal protections?', 'For each cabinet type, and for idle, typical, and design power usage, what do the 100% heat removal flow and inlet temperature curves look like?' and 'For idle, typical, and design power usages, how much heat load goes to the liquid cooling'.
attrs.remedy: Put these four questions into the IT equipment RFP verbatim. Without an excursion tolerance in magnitude AND duration, 'ride-through' has no pass criterion and the IST has no threshold.
attrs.ground_contact: EXTRACTED verbatim from the EE HPC WG liquid cooling controls whitepaper.

nodes.label: Independently controlled room units fight each other, and humidity sensor drift sustains the fight

attrs.missing_or_defect: 'Modular units are notorious for battling each other to maintain data center humidity set points. That is, one unit can be observed to be dehumidifying while an adjacent unit is humidifying.' And: 'Humidity sensor drift can also contribute to control problems if sensors are not regularly recalibrated.' LBNL's 2024 national report repeats the same observation when cautioning that modelled PUEs are optimistic.
attrs.remedy: Centralise humidity control on shared sensors and setpoints, put sensor recalibration on a schedule, and run coils above dewpoint (LBNL: 'usually by running chilled water temperatures above 50F') so the dehumidification never starts.
attrs.ground_contact: EXTRACTED from two LBNL documents. NOTE per rule 5: these are the same institution, so this is consistency, not independent corroboration.

nodes.label: Controlling on return air temperature makes a starved rack invisible to the plant

attrs.missing_or_defect: LBNL is explicit twice: 'Control supply temperature (and airflow) based on IT equipment intake air temperatures and not on the return temperature', and 'the temperature monitoring to control the air handlers should be located in areas in front of the computer equipment, not on a wall behind the equipment'. A return-controlled plant reports satisfied while a recirculating rack cooks, because the mixed return is the average of the problem and its surroundings.
attrs.remedy: Sensor placement is a resilience decision, not a commissioning detail. Specify intake sensing and, where available, onboard server sensors as the control input.
attrs.ground_contact: EXTRACTED verbatim from the LBNL/DOE Best Practices Guide.

nodes.label: The BMS is a networked control surface with a documented vulnerability history

attrs.missing_or_defect: CISA has published advisories against widely deployed building-automation middleware (Tridium Niagara), covering directory traversal and weak credential storage; subsequent research describes flaws enabling session hijack and command execution against systems lacking encryption or network segmentation, with the risk framed as compromise of HVAC and energy management infrastructure.
attrs.remedy: Segment the mechanical control network, treat BMS patching and credential management as in-scope for the campus security program, and require that no cooling protection interlock depends solely on a routable, internet-reachable control path.
attrs.ground_contact: Read the CISA advisory listing and summary; the vulnerability class is grounded, the data-centre-specific exploitation is inferred.

nodes.label: 60-90% liquid heat capture means the air plant remains mandatory and is what fails first
nodes.source_location: Reject heat to facility water systems

attrs.missing_or_defect: '60% to 90% of a liquid-cooled server's heat can be removed via the liquid, depending on the number of liquid-cooled components. The remaining heat is removed by air cooling (e.g., CRAC, CRAH, rear door heat exchanger).' At a 120 kW rack, a 20% air residual is 24 kW per rack of air cooling — more than a whole conventional rack.
attrs.remedy: Size, power and back up the residual air system as a critical system. It is routinely treated as a leftover, and it is the part of a liquid-cooled hall with the shortest ride-through.
attrs.ground_contact: EXTRACTED verbatim from Schneider WP133 v2; the 120 kW arithmetic is illustrative.

nodes.label: Facility water cannot be run directly through cold plates — the CDU exists to enforce that boundary

attrs.missing_or_defect: 'Direct-to-chip liquid-cooled servers have stringent requirements in water temperature, flowrate, and chemistry. This means that water from facility systems (e.g., a chiller) cannot run directly through a chip's cold plate. Doing so can corrode metals and tiny fluid channels within the cold plate.' The CDU's fluid-treatment function is stated as 'the filtration and chemistry requirements of the fluids in the TCS are more stringent than facility systems'.
attrs.remedy: The loop boundary is a hard requirement, not an architecture preference. Any value-engineering proposal that deletes the heat exchanger and couples the loops is an equipment-destroying change, not a saving.
attrs.ground_contact: EXTRACTED verbatim from Schneider WP133 v2.

nodes.label: Cold plate channels are hundreds of microns wide and biofilm is a worse insulator than scale

attrs.missing_or_defect: HTRI describes cold-plate heat exchangers with 'plates spaced only hundreds of microns apart', loops 'prone to calcium-carbonate precipitation and other forms of mineral scaling', and states that 'microbial films can be 10-100% more thermally resistant than calcium carbonate' and that 'because many data centers do not routinely monitor water quality, biofilm can develop undetected, making remediation of cold plate exchangers difficult'. It cites industry practice of 'a 25% PG / 75% water blend; concentrations below roughly 17% allow biofilm formation to accelerate', at a cost of '~8% reduction in heat capacity' plus pumping power.
attrs.remedy: Water quality monitoring is a protection system for the IT equipment, not a facilities chore. Specify sampling, action limits and side-stream filtration at RFP, and note the glycol concentration is simultaneously a biofouling control and a thermal derate.
attrs.ground_contact: EXTRACTED from a heat-transfer research organisation's public article. The authoritative numeric water-quality limits remain UNGROUNDED — see the water quality gap.

nodes.label: CDU form factor caps achievable rack density and fixes the failure domain
nodes.source_location: Step 2 - Choose CDU capacity and form factor

attrs.missing_or_defect: Rack-mounted CDUs 'limit maximum rack density to about 40 kW (L-A) and 80 kW (L-L)'; floor-mounted liquid-to-air reaches 'up to about 60 kW' and floor-mounted liquid-to-liquid ranges '300 kW to greater than 1 MW'. Schneider's implementation guidance is rack-mounted for '1 to 10 racks' and floor-mounted for 'more than 10 liquid-cooled racks'.
attrs.remedy: The CDU choice is a density ceiling and a blast-radius choice made simultaneously. Record both consequences when the choice is made, because only the density one gets discussed.
attrs.ground_contact: EXTRACTED verbatim from Schneider WP133 v2 (vendor-authored; capacities are market characterisations as of the 2024 edition).

nodes.label: A dedicated heat rejection loop lets liquid run hot and air run cold, which is what unlocks compressor-less hours

attrs.missing_or_defect: Schneider's dedicated-loop example uses 'a dry cooler with trim compressor... to provide a high supply water temperature (40C/104F) for liquid cooling, while a free-cooling chiller is used to provide a low chilled water temperature (20C/68F) for air cooling'. Advantages listed include 'high energy efficiency due to increased free cooling hours (mechanical cooling is not required in most cases except on hottest days)' and 'higher return water temperatures offer the opportunity for reuse'.
attrs.remedy: For a greenfield campus expecting significant liquid-cooled load, the dedicated loop is the architecture that pays; its cost is 'requires design of additional facility-level piping system' and 'longer deployment time', both of which are cheap at land-close and expensive later.
attrs.ground_contact: EXTRACTED verbatim from Schneider WP133 v2.

nodes.label: The cooling topology choice is fundamentally a site water-versus-energy trade, and site WUE alone misleads

attrs.missing_or_defect: 'Data centers employing water-cooled chiller systems without economizers exhibit the highest WUE, largely attributed to substantial cooling tower water usage.' But 'low site WUEs are [not] necessarily good... water-cooled chillers and other evaporation-based cooling systems are generally more energy efficient than an air-cooled chiller or other waterless systems. While air-cooled chillers use no water, they use more energy.' LBNL distinguishes site WUE from source WUE, which 'accounts for the water required to generate the electricity'.
attrs.remedy: Evaluate topologies on site WUE and source WUE and PUE together against the specific grid and the specific water source. A campus that optimises site WUE alone can increase total water consumption through its electricity.
attrs.ground_contact: EXTRACTED verbatim from the LBNL 2024 United States Data Center Energy Usage Report (2024-12-20). Water sourcing and rights are L1's scope; this finding is about the plant choice.

nodes.label: Reported hyperscale WUE for airside-economiser-plus-adiabatic plant is far above the modelled value

attrs.missing_or_defect: LBNL: 'Some hyperscale facilities report WUE values for similar systems of 0.1-0.3 L/kWh, which is much higher than the values simulated here, though the specifics of those systems are not known.' The simulations 'are set up such that the adiabatic cooling system is not used most of the year', which LBNL concedes 'might not be reflective of the true practices'.
attrs.remedy: Do not size a water budget from modelled WUE for adiabatic plant. Use reported operating values and state the assumed wet-mode hours explicitly.
attrs.ground_contact: EXTRACTED verbatim from LBNL 2024, including LBNL's own caveat on its model.

nodes.label: Modelled cooling performance assumes commissioning and as-designed operation, which LBNL says is rarely the case

attrs.missing_or_defect: Verbatim: 'Note that simulated PUEs assume systems are commissioned and operate as designed. This is rarely the case, and generally system performance does not meet design expectations.' The example given is the same one from the design guide: units fighting each other on humidity.
attrs.remedy: Treat every efficiency and capacity number in the design basis as conditional on commissioning evidence. This is the strongest open statement available that the commissioning gate is the load-bearing one, and it comes from a national laboratory, not a commissioning vendor.
attrs.ground_contact: EXTRACTED verbatim from LBNL 2024.

nodes.label: Water-side economiser viability is set by hours below a wet-bulb threshold and by the chilled water design temperature

attrs.missing_or_defect: 'Free cooling is usually best suited for climates that have wet bulb temperatures lower than 55F for 3,000 or more hours per year. It most effectively serves chilled water loops designed for 50F and above chilled water or lower temperature chilled water loops with significant surplus air handler capacity.'
attrs.remedy: The economiser decision is therefore downstream of two earlier decisions — the site (its wet bulb record) and the loop design temperature. Both are fixed early, so the economiser hours are effectively decided before anyone models them.
attrs.ground_contact: EXTRACTED verbatim from the LBNL/DOE Best Practices Guide.

nodes.label: Air-side economiser contamination risk is contested in practice while the filtration answer is stated as settled

attrs.missing_or_defect: LBNL states both that 'data center professionals are split in the perception of risk when using this strategy' and that 'if minimum efficiency reporting value (MERV) 13 filters are used, the negative effects of outside air pollutants are small', while adding that 'concern over contamination should be limited to unusually harsh environments'. The split is between practitioner risk appetite and the technical assessment, not between two technical assessments.

nodes.label: The HFC rule bans installation, not just manufacture — a compliant purchase can become a non-compliant install

attrs.missing_or_defect: Paragraph (c) prohibits any person from installing — or having installed 'through their position as a designer, owner, or operator' — restricted systems, and (c)(13) names 'data center, information technology equipment facility, and computer room cooling systems' at GWP 700 or greater. The building-permit extension in paragraph (d) is granted only to 'industrial process refrigeration systems with a January 1, 2026, compliance date, retail food-supermarket, cold storage warehouse, and ice rink subsectors' — the data centre subsector is NOT among them.
attrs.remedy: Check the install date against the rule, and do not assume a permit-based grandfather exists for data centre cooling. Verify the current text before relying on this — the part has been amended and reconsidered.
attrs.ground_contact: EXTRACTED verbatim from eCFR § 84.54 on 2026-08-13. The absence of the data centre subsector from paragraph (d) is an observation about the text as read, not a legal opinion.

nodes.label: Count mechanical redundancy only together with its control path and control power

attrs.missing_or_defect: N+2 chillers that cannot receive a run signal are N+0. Both major published incidents in this lineage's evidence base are of this exact shape: healthy machines, dead signalling.
attrs.remedy: Extend the cut-set model so that every mechanical component carries an edge to its controller, its controller's power source, and its permissive interlocks. Redundancy claims that do not survive that extension are not redundancy claims.
attrs.ground_contact: Synthesis of two operator-published incidents; converges with wave 1 L3's finding on control-plane failure bypassing mechanical redundancy.

nodes.label: A ride-through claim that has not survived a heat-loaded integrated systems test is an opinion

attrs.missing_or_defect: The only open procedure that can falsify a thermal ride-through claim requires design-load electrical load banks AND 'floor-standing heater load banks placed in the white space' dumping the same kW as the IT racks, instrumented at rack inlet on a fast time base. Anything less tests the electrical system and infers the thermal one.
attrs.remedy: Make heater load banks and rack-inlet instrumentation non-negotiable line items in the commissioning scope, and set the pass threshold from the lowest IT shutdown threshold in the planned fleet.
attrs.ground_contact: Grounded in a public commissioning field guide plus Dell's and Cundall's measured/modelled work.

nodes.label: Cooling is a distribution problem wearing a capacity problem's clothes

attrs.missing_or_defect: Every mechanism in this lineage that starves a rack — plenum negative pressure near the CRAH, cable congestion, tile moves, recirculation through unblanked slots, a single CDU's flow loss — is a distribution failure that the aggregate capacity number cannot see. LBNL states it directly for raised floors: conventional tile delivery 'can be ill-suited for responding to the resulting dynamic heat load without either over-cooling the space or starving some areas of sufficient cooling'.
attrs.remedy: Report cooling health as a distribution metric across the rack population (e.g. RCI, or worst-rack inlet), never as installed tons versus IT kW.
attrs.ground_contact: EXTRACTED verbatim from the LBNL/DOE Best Practices Guide, section 5.8.

nodes.label: Circulating claim: cooling failures cause nearly one in five data centre outages

attrs.missing_or_defect: The figure circulates widely in vendor and trade material. The primary source it traces to (Uptime Institute's Annual Outage Analysis) is paywalled and was NOT read, so the definition — which outages, whose population, what counts as cooling-caused, which year — is unknown.
attrs.remedy: REJECT as evidence. If a cooling-share-of-outages number is needed for the proposal, a human must purchase and read the Uptime report and record the definition alongside the number.
attrs.ground_contact: UNGROUNDED — repetition across vendor pages is circulation, not corroboration (binding rule 5). No primary source was reached.

nodes.label: Circulating claim: a data hall heats at roughly 1-3.5 degrees F per minute after cooling loss
nodes.source_location: search-result snippets from HVAC trade pages

attrs.missing_or_defect: Trade pages quote 'about 1 to 2 degrees Fahrenheit per minute' and 'about 3.5 degrees (2 degrees C) per minute'. No source states its density, room volume, containment, or whether air movers were running — the four variables Dell's instrumented tests show dominate the answer. As stated, the claim is unfalsifiable and contradicts the measured two-regime curve shape.
attrs.remedy: REJECT as a design input. Use Dell's measured curves for the mechanism and a site-specific transient model for the number.
attrs.ground_contact: UNGROUNDED — unsourced trade-press figures with no stated test conditions.

nodes.label: Target curriculum has zero coverage of thermal ride-through or continuous cooling

attrs.missing_or_defect: Confirmed in the lineage brief: 0 of 121 cooling items mention ride-through or continuous cooling. The curriculum therefore teaches cooling as a steady-state capacity subject, which is precisely the framing under which every incident in this lineage's evidence base occurred.
attrs.remedy: Add a ride-through module built on the mechanism chain in this fragment: two-regime curve, four purchase levers, restart time as the binding constraint, restart lockout, load shed as the exit, and the IST as the only proof.
attrs.ground_contact: Gap identified while attempting to ground this lineage; see missing_or_defect for what was reachable and what was not.

nodes.label: No open, instrumented ride-through dataset exists for 100+ kW liquid-cooled racks

Cundall's 2026 work is high-density and liquid-aware but publishes conclusions, not data, and its model is proprietary. Nothing open covers the regime the campus will actually operate in.
attrs.remedy: Either commission site-specific transient modelling with validation against the IST (and keep the validation data), or treat every ride-through number in the design basis as unvalidated.

A chilled-water plant serving a data hall is plausibly described by more than one of these and the text read does not resolve it.
attrs.remedy: Get a written regulatory determination before the chiller order, not after. The dates differ by a year and the installation prohibition has no permit-based extension for data centres.

So the operational decay of containment cannot be priced against the resilience it was credited with.
attrs.remedy: Instrument containment leakage (blower-door style or tracer) at handover and periodically, and make the transient model re-runnable against a measured leakage input.

attrs.missing_or_defect: Both are described taxonomically in every source read and quantitatively in none. Two-phase immersion in particular has a passive condensing cycle that plausibly gives it the best ride-through of any option, and there is no open measurement of it.
attrs.remedy: If either is a candidate, require the vendor to supply instrumented loss-of-power thermal data and treat its absence as a disqualifying gap.

nodes.label: No source read addresses common control power for the mechanical control plane

attrs.remedy: Write the requirement locally: every controller, VFD, actuator and field network segment required for cooling recovery sits on protected power, on a path independent of the plant it commands, and is exercised in the IST.

nodes.label: Accreditation, certification, licensure and 'recognised' are taught as synonyms

attrs.missing_or_defect: No data-centre programme surveyed teaches the four-way distinction. Learners emerge unable to parse the credentials they are being sold.
attrs.remedy: Teach the chain explicitly: accreditation body -> certification body -> certified organisation; licensure as a separate statutory grant; 'recognised' as an unclaimed marketing word.
attrs.ground_contact: UKAS defines conformity assessment as 'the demonstration that what is being supplied meets the requirements specified or claimed'; accreditation attests the certification body, certification attests the client

nodes.label: Who is entitled to issue a conformity award is never taught

nodes.label: Certificate expiry and surveillance regimes are never taught
