attrs.ground_contact: Absence verified against the 804-item bank, the objectives registry and the 14 modules

nodes.label: The commissioning to operations handover boundary is not taught

attrs.ground_contact: Absence verified against the 804-item bank, the objectives registry and the 14 modules

nodes.label: Certification is taught without distinguishing it from commissioning

attrs.ground_contact: Read verbatim from DOE O 422.1.

nodes.label: Warning and caution placement rule

attrs.missing_or_defect: Warnings and cautions complete on one page, immediately before and on the same page as the affected step, written as statements not commands.
attrs.remedy: Enforce in the procedure template; a warning on the previous page is a warning that was not read.
attrs.ground_contact: Read verbatim from DOE-STD-1029-92.

nodes.label: Place-keeping

attrs.missing_or_defect: Physically marking completed steps to prevent omission and to survive interruption.
attrs.remedy: Mandatory for use-each-time procedures; it is what makes a paused MOP resumable across a shift change.
attrs.ground_contact: Read verbatim from DOE-HDBK-1028 Vol 2.

nodes.label: 29 CFR 1910.147 expressly excludes electrical-hazard exposure in electric-utilization installations

attrs.missing_or_defect: 1910.147(a)(1)(ii) states the standard does not cover '(D) Exposure to electrical hazards from work on, near, or with conductors or equipment in electric-utilization installations, which is covered by subpart S of this part'. A data centre's switchgear, UPS, PDU and busway are an electric-utilization installation.
attrs.remedy: Scope the energy-control programme across 1910.147 (machines, stored energy) and Subpart S / 1910.333 (electrical hazard), using the 1910.333(b)(2) NOTE 2 bridge to run one compliant programme.
attrs.ground_contact: Read verbatim from the GPO CFR text.

nodes.label: A campus with its own substation runs three overlapping OSHA regimes

attrs.missing_or_defect: 1910.269 covers utility-side power generation, transformation, transmission and distribution installations 'accessible only to qualified employees'; 1910.147 excludes installations under the exclusive control of electric utilities; Subpart S covers the utilization side.
attrs.remedy: Map every asset on the campus one-line to its governing regime before writing a single procedure.
attrs.ground_contact: Scope clauses read verbatim from osha.gov and the CFR; the mapping to a campus is inferred.

nodes.label: Deenergise-before-work is the legal default, with only two narrow exceptions

attrs.missing_or_defect: 'Live parts to which an employee may be exposed shall be deenergized before the employee works on or near them, unless the employer can demonstrate that deenergizing introduces additional or increased hazards or is infeasible due to equipment design or operational limitations.'
attrs.remedy: Treat energised work as an exception requiring a demonstrated justification, not as a normal operating mode.
attrs.ground_contact: Read verbatim from the GPO CFR text.

nodes.label: Whether an IT load is a 'continuous industrial process' under the infeasibility exception is unsettled

attrs.missing_or_defect: NOTE 2 gives as an infeasibility example 'work on circuits that form an integral part of a continuous industrial process in a chemical plant'. No public OSHA interpretation reachable in this pass settles whether an IT load qualifies.
attrs.remedy: Do not build an operations model that depends on the permissive reading; design isolation in instead.
attrs.ground_contact: The regulatory note is read verbatim; the applicability question is genuinely open and is marked as such.

nodes.label: Control circuit devices and interlocks may not be used as isolation

attrs.missing_or_defect: 'Control circuit devices, such as push buttons, selector switches, and interlocks, may not be used as the sole means for deenergizing circuits or equipment. Interlocks for electric equipment may not be used as a substitute for lockout and tagging procedures.'
attrs.remedy: Putting a UPS into maintenance bypass from its HMI is not isolation; the procedure must reach a physical disconnecting means.
attrs.ground_contact: Read verbatim from the GPO CFR text.

nodes.label: Verification of a deenergised condition must explicitly test for backfeed

attrs.missing_or_defect: 'The test shall also determine if any energized condition exists as a result of inadvertently induced voltage or unrelated voltage backfeed even though specific parts of the circuit have been deenergized and presumed to be safe.'
attrs.remedy: In dual-corded A/B topologies with downstream static and rack-mount transfer switches, make the backfeed check a named step.
attrs.ground_contact: Read verbatim from the GPO CFR text.

nodes.label: The exception permitting an undocumented energy-control procedure is unreachable in a data centre

attrs.missing_or_defect: The exception requires all of eight conditions including no potential for stored or residual energy and a single readily identifiable energy source. Data-centre plant satisfies neither.
attrs.remedy: Every maintainable asset needs a written, equipment-specific energy-control procedure.
attrs.ground_contact: The exception text read verbatim; the inapplicability conclusion is inferred.

nodes.label: The energy-control procedure must be inspected at least annually

attrs.missing_or_defect: 'The employer shall conduct a periodic inspection of the energy control procedure at least annually to ensure that the procedure and the requirements of this standard are being followed.'
attrs.remedy: Schedule the inspection as a recurring CMMS task with a named authorised employee as subject, not as an audit line item.
attrs.ground_contact: Read verbatim from the GPO CFR text.

nodes.label: On-site and outside employers must inform each other of their lockout/tagout procedures

attrs.missing_or_defect: 'Whenever outside servicing personnel are to be engaged in activities covered by the scope and application of this standard, the on-site employer and the outside employer shall inform each other of their respective lockout or tagout procedures.'
attrs.remedy: Make procedure exchange a precondition of site access for every OEM and service contractor.
attrs.ground_contact: Read verbatim from the GPO CFR text.

nodes.label: Level of use is the procedure attribute that decides whether the paper is open during the work

attrs.missing_or_defect: DOE O 422.1 requires 'specified and defined procedure use requirements, i.e., reader-worker method, reference use only, use-each-time, and emergency response'.
attrs.remedy: Print level of use on the cover of every MOP, SOP and EOP.
attrs.ground_contact: Read verbatim from DOE O 422.1.

nodes.label: Procedures use imperative commands; requirements documents use 'shall'

attrs.missing_or_defect: 'In procedures governed by the guidelines in this writer's guide, this type of sentence is not used to express required actions. Imperative sentences (commands) are used instead.'
attrs.remedy: Reject any MOP written in 'shall' prose; it is a specification wearing a procedure's cover page.
attrs.ground_contact: Read verbatim from DOE-STD-1029-92.

nodes.label: An industry study attributed one-fourth of human performance events to missing warnings and cautions

attrs.missing_or_defect: 'An industry study of significant events attributed one-fourth of all human performance events to a failure to provide proper warnings and cautions.'
attrs.remedy: Treat warning/caution authoring as a first-class step in procedure development, with a technical-specialist review.
attrs.ground_contact: Read verbatim from DOE-STD-1029-92. The underlying industry study is not named in the standard and was not read.

nodes.label: 'Unexpected results are achieved after performing the step' is itself a stop condition

attrs.missing_or_defect: The handbook lists seven conditions requiring the worker to STOP, place equipment in a safe condition and contact a supervisor; unexpected result is one of them, alongside step-not-performable-as-written and procedure-conflicts-with-another.
attrs.remedy: Print the seven stop conditions inside the cover of every procedure; it is the cheapest abort criterion available.
attrs.ground_contact: Read verbatim from DOE-HDBK-1028 Vol 2.

nodes.label: Following a procedure without question does not guarantee safety

attrs.missing_or_defect: 'Procedure quality is paramount to safety and reliability. Following the procedure without question does not guarantee safety because procedures sometimes contain hidden flaws... Experience has shown that procedures do not always contain sufficient information.'
attrs.remedy: Pair procedure adherence with a questioning attitude and an easy, blame-free route to stop and raise a defect.
attrs.ground_contact: Read verbatim from DOE-HDBK-1028 Vol 2.

nodes.label: Permit systems imposed without consultation make procedural violations more likely

attrs.missing_or_defect: 'Imposing systems without consultation can lead to procedures that do not reflect the needs of maintenance staff, for example. Procedural violations are then more likely.'
attrs.remedy: Consult the maintainers when designing the permit system; violation is a design output, not only a personal failing.
attrs.ground_contact: Read verbatim from HSE HSG250.

nodes.label: A permit-to-work system must provide formal handover and hand-back procedures

attrs.missing_or_defect: HSG250 lists 'providing a formal handover procedure for use when a permit is issued for a period longer than one shift' and 'providing a formal hand-back procedure to ensure that the part of the plant affected by the work is in a safe condition and ready for reinstatement'.
attrs.remedy: Both are routinely omitted in data-centre permit forms; add them as mandatory sections.
attrs.ground_contact: Read verbatim from HSE HSG250.

nodes.label: The average facility runs a majority-reactive maintenance mix

attrs.missing_or_defect: The referenced study breaks the average maintenance programme down as more than 55% reactive, 31% preventive, 12% predictive, 2% other.
attrs.remedy: Use as the baseline against which to justify funding a predictive programme.
attrs.ground_contact: Read verbatim from the DOE/PNNL O&M Best Practices Guide Release 3.0. The underlying winter-2000 study is cited there but was not read.

nodes.label: Top-performing facilities run a predictive-dominant mix: under 10% reactive

attrs.missing_or_defect: '<10% Reactive; 25% to 35% Preventive; 45% to 55% Predictive.'
attrs.remedy: Adopt as the contractual target mix for the O&M provider.
attrs.ground_contact: Read verbatim from the DOE/PNNL O&M Best Practices Guide Release 3.0.

nodes.label: Seven O&M benchmark metrics are specific enough to write into a contract

attrs.missing_or_defect: Equipment availability >95%; schedule compliance >90%; emergency maintenance <10%; maintenance overtime <5%; PM completion >90%; PM budget 15-18% of maintenance cost; PdM budget 10-12%.
attrs.remedy: Put emergency-maintenance <10% and PM-completion >90% in the O&M agreement; both are auditable from the CMMS.
attrs.ground_contact: Read verbatim from the DOE/PNNL O&M Best Practices Guide Release 3.0 table 3.1.1.

nodes.label: Scheduled overhaul can increase the overall failure rate

attrs.missing_or_defect: 'In many cases scheduled overhaul increases the overall failure rate by introducing a high infant mortality rate into an otherwise stable system.'
attrs.remedy: Move static electrical plant and its controls off calendar-based intrusive PM and onto condition monitoring.
attrs.ground_contact: Read verbatim from the NASA RCM Guide for Facilities and Collateral Equipment (2008).

nodes.label: Across three studies, 77 to 92 percent of failures were random rather than age-related

attrs.missing_or_defect: 'In these three studies, random failures are between 77 and 92 percent of the total failures and age-related failure characteristics for the remaining 8 to 23 percent.'
attrs.remedy: Time-based intervals are justified only for the minority of items with a demonstrated wear-out age.
attrs.ground_contact: Read verbatim from the NASA RCM Guide. The per-pattern percentage table is deliberately NOT reproduced: the column-to-pattern mapping did not survive text extraction cleanly.

nodes.label: 'Systems which failure may be induced by incorrect preventive maintenance' is a named predictive-maintenance application
nodes.source_location: table 5.5.1 as reproduced in the O&M Guide

attrs.missing_or_defect: The RCM element-application hierarchy lists that phrase under predictive element applications, alongside equipment with random failure patterns and critical equipment.
attrs.remedy: Use this row as the written justification for moving UPS, switchgear relays, transfer switch logic and controllers off intrusive PM.
attrs.ground_contact: Read verbatim from the DOE/PNNL O&M Guide table 5.5.1, adapted there from NASA 2000.

nodes.label: A master equipment list and criticality ranking are the first two steps of any maintenance strategy
nodes.source_location: section 5.6 as reproduced in the O&M Guide

attrs.missing_or_defect: 'Develop a Master equipment list identifying the equipment in your facility' then 'Prioritize the listed components based on importance or criticality', with a 1-6 weighting from Emergency (life, health, safety risk / mission criticality) to Deferred.
attrs.remedy: Make both a handover deliverable rather than a first-year operations project.
attrs.ground_contact: Read verbatim from the DOE/PNNL O&M Guide, adapted there from NASA 2000.

nodes.label: Manufacturer PM intervals are shaped by warranty exposure, not by the item's failure distribution

attrs.missing_or_defect: The RCM hierarchy lists 'Manufacturer recommendations' under preventive element applications, i.e. as a basis distinct from observed condition.
attrs.remedy: Record the basis of every interval explicitly; where vendor and condition disagree, the disagreement is the deliverable.
attrs.ground_contact: The table row is read verbatim; the liability-shaping characterisation is inferred.

nodes.label: If the one-line has no physical isolation point that leaves the load served, lawful maintenance requires a load outage

attrs.missing_or_defect: Deenergise-first is the default; control devices and interlocks are not isolation; a qualified person must test and verify including backfeed. Taken together these make concurrent maintainability a property of the physical topology, not of the operations team.
attrs.remedy: Add an isolation register to the electrical design review: for every maintainable device, name the disconnecting means and state whether the load stays served.
attrs.ground_contact: Derived by combining three provisions read verbatim; the derivation is this lineage's, not OSHA's.

nodes.label: The FirstEnergy alarm processor failed at 14:14 EDT and nobody was told, including by the system itself

attrs.missing_or_defect: '14:14 EDT: FE alarm and logging software failed. Neither FE's control room operators nor FE's IT EMS support personnel were aware of the alarm failure.'
attrs.remedy: Require a monitoring stack to alarm its own failure; the report states such configuration exists and that FE's EMS did not have it.
attrs.ground_contact: Read verbatim from the U.S.-Canada Power System Outage Task Force Final Report (April 2004).

nodes.label: An alarm system can be set up to alarm operators if the alarm system itself fails
nodes.source_location: chapter 5, Failure of FE's Alarm System

attrs.missing_or_defect: 'In the same way that an alarm system can inform operators about the failure of key grid facilities, it can also be set up to alarm them if the alarm system itself fails to perform properly. FE's EMS did not have such a notification system.'
attrs.remedy: This sentence is the specification clause. Put it in the DCIM/BMS/EPMS requirements verbatim.
attrs.ground_contact: Read verbatim from the Outage Task Force report.

nodes.label: Failover propagated the fault: the stalled application moved intact to the backup, which failed 13 minutes later

attrs.missing_or_defect: 'because the alarm application moved intact onto the backup while still stalled and ineffective, the backup server failed 13 minutes later, at 14:54 EDT.'
attrs.remedy: Ask the monitoring vendor what the standby node does NOT inherit at failover; hardware redundancy does not cover application state.
attrs.ground_contact: Read verbatim from the Outage Task Force report.

nodes.label: A warm reboot showed all expected processes running while the alarm system stayed frozen

attrs.missing_or_defect: 'Startup diagnostics monitored during that reboot verified that the computer and all expected processes were running... However, although the server and its applications were again running, the alarm system remained frozen and non-functional... The IT staff did not confirm that the alarm system was again working properly with the control room operators.'
attrs.remedy: The post-maintenance acceptance criterion is an operator confirming a test alarm, not a service showing as running.
attrs.ground_contact: Read verbatim from the Outage Task Force report.

nodes.label: IT support was auto-paged twice and did not notify the control room

attrs.missing_or_defect: 'When the back-up server failed, it too sent an auto-page to FE's IT staff. They did not notify control room operators of the problem.'
attrs.remedy: Write a standing notification rule: any monitoring-system fault notifies the operating shift, not only the support team.
attrs.ground_contact: Read verbatim from the Outage Task Force report.

nodes.label: Degraded instrumentation is more dangerous than absent instrumentation

attrs.missing_or_defect: Screen refresh rates 'normally 1 to 3 seconds' slowed 'to as long as 59 seconds per screen', and the strip-chart printers continued to scroll on frozen data.
attrs.remedy: Specify explicit degraded-mode indication; an instrument that looks alive while conveying nothing defeats every human control.
attrs.ground_contact: Read verbatim from the Outage Task Force report.

nodes.label: The Task Force's 'inadequate situational awareness' causes read as a monitoring procurement checklist
nodes.source_location: Causes of the Blackout's Initiation, Group 2

attrs.missing_or_defect: '(B) FE lacked procedures to ensure that its operators were continually aware of the functional state of their critical monitoring tools.' '(C) ...did not have effective internal communications procedures.' '(D) FE lacked procedures to test effectively the functional state of its monitoring tools after repairs were made.' '(E) FE did not have additional or back-up monitoring tools...'
attrs.remedy: Convert B, C, D and E into four named requirements in the monitoring specification.
attrs.ground_contact: Read verbatim from the Outage Task Force report.

nodes.label: Operators read the absence of alarms as evidence that conditions were safe

attrs.missing_or_defect: 'Continuing on in the belief that their system was satisfactory, lacking any alarms from their EMS to the contrary... FE control room operators were subsequently surprised when they began receiving telephone calls from other locations and information sources... that conflicted with FE's system operators' understanding of the situation.'
attrs.remedy: Write into the EOP: an external report that conflicts with your instrumentation is evidence about your instrumentation.
attrs.ground_contact: Read verbatim from the Outage Task Force report.

nodes.label: Published alarm-rate targets exist: one alarm per ten minutes in steady state

attrs.missing_or_defect: 'the long-term average alarm rate during normal operation should be no more than one every ten minutes; and no more than ten displayed in the first ten minutes following a major plant upset'.
attrs.remedy: Adopt as the acceptance criterion for the commissioned alarm configuration.
attrs.ground_contact: Read verbatim from HSE CHIS6, which attributes the figures to EEMUA 191 page 37. EEMUA 191 was NOT read.

nodes.label: Alarm priorities should be proportioned roughly 5% high, 15% medium, 80% low across about three priorities

attrs.missing_or_defect: 'Use about three priorities. Base priorities on the potential consequences if the operator fails to respond. Prioritise proportionately, eg 5% high priority, 15% medium, and 80% low.'
attrs.remedy: Audit the delivered configuration against this distribution before accepting the monitoring system.
attrs.ground_contact: Read verbatim from HSE CHIS6, attributed there to EEMUA 191 page 65. EEMUA 191 was NOT read.

nodes.label: Process status indicators should not be designated as alarms

attrs.missing_or_defect: 'Are they all necessary, requiring operator action? (Note: process status indicators should not be designated as alarms.)' and 'eliminate/review alarms with no defined operator response'.
attrs.remedy: Apply the operator-action test to every configured alarm; it removes most data-centre alarm noise on first contact.
attrs.ground_contact: Read verbatim from HSE CHIS6.

nodes.label: Thorough alarm review can cost more than one shift per alarm

attrs.missing_or_defect: 'A quick first-pass review may cover perhaps 50 alarms per shift but a thorough review and redesign may take more than 1 shift per alarm.'
attrs.remedy: Budget rationalisation as a programme before the point schedule is frozen, not as a punch-list item afterwards.
attrs.ground_contact: Read verbatim from HSE CHIS6.

nodes.label: At Milford Haven two operators faced 275 alarms in the last 11 minutes before the explosion

attrs.missing_or_defect: 'In the last 11 minutes before the explosion the two operators had to recognise, acknowledge and act on 275 alarms.'
attrs.remedy: Use as the concrete anchor for what alarm flood means; it is why rate targets exist.
attrs.ground_contact: Read verbatim from HSE CHIS6 summarising HSE's own investigation report.

nodes.label: Incidents should not be handled first-come, first-served

attrs.missing_or_defect: 'Prioritizing the handling of the incident is perhaps the most critical decision point in the incident handling process. Incidents should not be handled on a first-come, first-served basis as a result of resource limitations.'
attrs.remedy: Publish the severity scale before the first incident; it is a resource-allocation instrument, not a label.
attrs.ground_contact: Read verbatim from NIST SP 800-61r2.

nodes.label: Severity is better expressed on orthogonal axes than as a single number

attrs.missing_or_defect: Functional impact (None/Low/Medium/High), information impact, and recoverability effort (Regular/Supplemented/Extended/Not Recoverable) are rated separately and combined.
attrs.remedy: For a facility, substitute a safety-impact axis for information impact: functional x safety x recoverability.
attrs.ground_contact: Axes read verbatim from NIST SP 800-61r2; the safety substitution is this lineage's.

nodes.label: An incident process needs a written path for when nobody responds

attrs.missing_or_defect: 'The escalation process should state how long a person should wait for a response and what to do if no response occurs.'
attrs.remedy: Specify the timeout and the next name in the chain; at 03:00 the on-call may simply not answer.
attrs.ground_contact: Read verbatim from NIST SP 800-61r2.

nodes.label: The incident Safety Officer stops or prevents unsafe acts, independently of the commander

attrs.missing_or_defect: 'The Safety Officer stops and/or prevents unsafe acts during the incident.'
attrs.remedy: During a 03:00 restoration the pressure to close a breaker is enormous; the IC is the wrong person to also hold the veto.
attrs.ground_contact: Read verbatim from FEMA NIMS 2017.

nodes.label: Unified Command, not single command, is the normal case for a campus incident

attrs.missing_or_defect: 'When more than one agency has incident jurisdiction, or when incidents cross political jurisdictions, the use of Unified Command enables multiple organizations to' act jointly under 'a single Incident Action Plan'.
attrs.remedy: Facility operator, tenant, utility and OEM field service each hold jurisdiction over part of a campus incident.
attrs.ground_contact: Read verbatim from FEMA NIMS 2017; the campus mapping is inferred.

nodes.label: Incident information is released under the Incident Commander's approval, with one voice
nodes.source_location: ICS Command Staff, Public Information Officer

attrs.missing_or_defect: 'All PIOs should work in a unified manner, speaking with one voice, and ensure that all messaging is consistent. The Incident Commander or Unified Command approves the release of incident-related information.'
attrs.remedy: Name the communications role in the facility incident process; PDX-04 shows the cost of leaving it implicit.
attrs.ground_contact: Read verbatim from FEMA NIMS 2017.

nodes.label: NIST's lessons-learned question set is a ready-made postmortem agenda

attrs.missing_or_defect: 'Exactly what happened, and at what times?'; 'Were the documented procedures followed? Were they adequate?'; 'What information was needed sooner?'; 'Were any steps or actions taken that might have inhibited the recovery?'; plus corrective actions and future precursors. 'The meeting should be held within several days of the end of the incident.'
attrs.remedy: Adopt verbatim as the postmortem agenda; it is free to redistribute, unlike the vendor write-ups.
attrs.ground_contact: Read verbatim from NIST SP 800-61r2.

nodes.label: Facility incident timelines come from three clocks that disagree

attrs.missing_or_defect: NIST requires 'a formal chronology of events (including timestamped information such as log data from systems)'. In a facility these come from the EPMS event log, the BMS trend and the operator's written log.
attrs.remedy: Specify time synchronisation across EPMS, BMS, DCIM and the log system; reconcile the three clocks as step one of every investigation.
attrs.ground_contact: The NIST requirement is read verbatim; the three-clock observation is inferred from the DCIM/BMS/EPMS split.

nodes.label: PDX-04's overnight shift was security plus a technician one week into the job

attrs.missing_or_defect: 'The overnight staffing at the site did not include an experienced operations or electrical expert - the overnight shift consisted of security and an unaccompanied technician who had only been on the job for a week.'
attrs.remedy: Specify minimum on-shift qualification contractually; this is what unspecified looks like.
attrs.ground_contact: Read verbatim from Cloudflare's public postmortem. Single-party account of a third party's facility.

nodes.label: The facility failed over to generator power and did not tell the tenant

attrs.missing_or_defect: 'Counter to best practices, Flexential did not inform Cloudflare that they had failed over to generator power.' The first message from the facility arrived at 12:28 UTC; total power loss was at 11:44 UTC, and the tenant learned from its own routers going offline.
attrs.remedy: Make transfer to any non-normal electrical configuration a notifiable event with a stated deadline.
attrs.ground_contact: Read verbatim from Cloudflare's public postmortem. Single-party account; the facility operator's response was not obtainable.

nodes.label: An unusual operating configuration was in force because of a grid-services commercial arrangement

attrs.missing_or_defect: 'It is also unusual that Flexential ran both the one remaining utility feed and the generators at the same time', in the context of a programme under which 'the power company helps maintain the generators and supplies fuel'.
attrs.remedy: Audit whether any revenue arrangement changes the normal operating configuration, and whether the operating procedures reflect it.
attrs.ground_contact: Read verbatim from Cloudflare's public postmortem.

nodes.label: PDX-04 was described in the postmortem as certified to a concurrently-maintainable design tier

attrs.missing_or_defect: The postmortem states the site's 'design was certified Tier III'.
attrs.remedy: Read a tier certificate as a claim about documented topology, not about the configuration in force on the night.
attrs.ground_contact: Read verbatim from Cloudflare's public postmortem. The Uptime Tier Standard itself was NOT read.

nodes.label: A single transformer ground fault shut down all generators and then all customer power

attrs.missing_or_defect: 'At approximately 11:40 UTC, there was a ground fault on a PGE transformer at PDX-04... the protective measure also shut down all of PDX-04's generators.' 'Between 11:44 and 12:01 UTC... the UPS batteries ran out of power and all customers of the data center lost power.'
attrs.remedy: Trace the protection scheme's common-cause reach across generation and utility, not only across feeders.
attrs.ground_contact: Read verbatim from Cloudflare's public postmortem.

nodes.label: Observed UPS autonomy at PDX-04 was about four minutes

attrs.missing_or_defect: 'In reality, the batteries started to fail after only 4 minutes based on what we observed from our own equipment failing.'
attrs.remedy: Treat autonomy as a measured, trended quantity: impedance trending plus periodic discharge test against the commissioning baseline.
attrs.ground_contact: Read verbatim from Cloudflare's public postmortem.

nodes.label: The whole-facility failure mode had never been exercised

attrs.missing_or_defect: 'However, we had never tested fully taking the entire PDX-04 facility offline. As a result, we had missed the importance of some of these dependencies.'
attrs.remedy: Schedule facility-level failure drills, including full site isolation, against the EOPs.
attrs.ground_contact: Read verbatim from Cloudflare's public postmortem.

nodes.label: No amount of counselling, training or motivation can alter a person's fallibility

attrs.missing_or_defect: 'People are fallible, and even the best people make mistakes. Error is universal. No one is immune regardless of age, experience, or educational level... No amount of counseling, training, or motivation can alter a person's fallibility.'
attrs.remedy: Design controls into the work, not into the worker; the second principle is that error-likely situations are predictable, manageable and preventable.
attrs.ground_contact: Read verbatim from DOE-HDBK-1028-2009 Vol 1.

nodes.label: Competence does not guarantee positive control

attrs.missing_or_defect: 'An unsafe personal dependency exists when an individual relies on his or her personal experience, proficiency, or qualifications to maintain control. Because past practices have not led to a problem, the individual becomes indifferent toward the need for care and attention. Competence does not guarantee positive control... Of particular concern is overconfidence in one's own ability at a critical step, inhibiting the rigorous use of human performance tools.'
attrs.remedy: This is why senior technicians produce incidents; the counter is observed tool use at critical steps, not more seniority.
attrs.ground_contact: Read verbatim from DOE-HDBK-1028-2009 Vol 1.

nodes.label: Error precursors fall into four categories with ranked common members

attrs.missing_or_defect: Task Demands, Individual Capabilities, Work Environment and Human Nature, each with eight ranked precursors; the lists include time pressure, irreversible actions, unfamiliarity with task, illness or fatigue, distractions, departure from routine, out-of-service instrumentation, hidden system response, complacency and mind-set.
attrs.remedy: Run the four categories as a sweep in the pre-job brief; most of the top precursors are structurally present in an out-of-hours MOP.
attrs.ground_contact: Read verbatim from DOE-HDBK-1028-2009 Vol 1.

nodes.label: Irreversible actions are singled out as often overlooked

attrs.missing_or_defect: 'Irreversible actions are not necessarily precursors to error, but are often overlooked, leading to preventable events. It is included in this list because of its importance.'
attrs.remedy: Tag irreversible steps explicitly in every procedure and put a hold point before each.
attrs.ground_contact: Read verbatim from DOE-HDBK-1028-2009 Vol 1.

nodes.label: Shift-change continuity of lockout/tagout protection is legally required

attrs.missing_or_defect: 'Specific procedures shall be utilized during shift or personnel changes to ensure the continuity of lockout or tagout protection, including provision for the orderly transfer of lockout or tagout device protection between off-going and oncoming employees.'
attrs.remedy: Handover is a mandated procedure whenever an isolation spans the change, not a courtesy.
attrs.ground_contact: Read verbatim from the GPO CFR text.

nodes.label: Turnover exists so the on-coming operator can build an accurate mental model before taking responsibility

attrs.missing_or_defect: 'A turnover provides time for the on-coming individual(s) to establish an accurate mental model of the work activity (situation awareness) before assuming responsibilities and commencing work.'
attrs.remedy: Judge a handover by whether the on-coming person can state the current state unprompted, not by whether words were exchanged.
attrs.ground_contact: Read verbatim from DOE-HDBK-1028 Vol 2.

nodes.label: The turnover content list is eight specific items, including procedures in use and last step completed

attrs.missing_or_defect: Job status and equipment status with parameter values; schedule changes and parallel activities; objectives and milestones; 'Procedures being used and last step(s) completed'; problems and unusual system lineups; 'Critical steps, possible error-likely situations, countermeasures, and contingencies'; resource availability; key contacts.
attrs.remedy: Use as the turnover template; the fourth and sixth items are the ones data-centre handovers omit.
attrs.ground_contact: Read verbatim from DOE-HDBK-1028 Vol 2.

nodes.label: Turnover method requires face-to-face exchange, independent log review and a joint walkdown

attrs.missing_or_defect: Principals meet 'face to face using formal three-way communication on critical information'; the on-coming person 'independently reviews the turnover log... checking for consistency and accuracy of information before assuming responsibility'; both walk down the work location together; responsibility is then officially transferred.
attrs.remedy: Three distinct acts, none of which substitutes for another.

Uptime: 'TIA approaches availability in terms of a checklist/component count, which does not ensure how the subsystems are tied together to deliver uptime in multiple operation modes (standard, maintenance, post-fault)' and 'We have intentionally refrained from developing a "design manual" or checklist to achieve a target Uptime Institute Tier level.' Outcome/performance evaluation vs prescriptive conformity assessment.

AXIS 5 - ONE RATING VS MANY. EN 50600 defines availability classes SEPARATELY for 2-2 electrical, 2-3 mechanical and 2-4 cabling, so 'AC4 electrical, AC2 mechanical' is a well-formed statement. Uptime awards one site rating governed by the weakest subsystem ('if you have a Concurrently Maintainable electrical infrastructure but only a single distribution path mechanical system ... "Tier III" can only lead to ultimate disappointment'). A bare 'Class 4' discards qualifiers that 'Tier IV' would not have permitted.

AXIS 9 - CLASSIFICATION GEOMETRY. TIA-942 issues Rating levels over four facility subsystems under a licensed CB scheme. EN 50600 splits the question into three ORTHOGONAL dimensions - Availability Classes, Protection Classes, Granularity Levels - with requirements conditional on the operator's risk analysis. 'Rated-3' is a single ordinal; the EN 50600 equivalent is a vector, and the two cannot be equated element-wise.

AXIS 11 - RETIRED CLAIM STILL IN CIRCULATION. The 99.67/99.75/99.98/99.99 table was read verbatim in a document uploaded 2023-07, but Uptime states 'In 2009, Uptime Institute removed all references to "expected downtime per year" when using the Tier Standard. The current Tier Standard of Topology does not assign availability predictions to Tier levels.' The claim is contradicted by its own purported authority.

AXIS 12 - STS AND TIER ELIGIBILITY. Schneider WP75 Table 1 maps 'Distributed redundant' to Tier III. Uptime's dual-corded article records a large-STS architecture where an 'STS-PDU fault affecting one-third of its IT equipment' rendered the facility unavailable and states this approach 'does not meet Tier III or Tier IV criteria'. Two public sources give opposite answers to 'is distributed-redundant-with-STS a Tier III topology?'

AXIS 13 - CONFIGURATION-TO-TIER MAPPING. Any table mapping a named UPS configuration to a Tier presupposes that configuration determines Tier. Uptime: 'Increasing the component count does not determine or guarantee achievement of any specific Tier level, because Tiers also includes evaluation of distribution pathways and other system elements', and Tier Certification 'is not a checklist or cookbook'.
Uptime stating in its own publication that the two systems are neither collaborative nor synonymous.
The conflation gap exists because the market treats as equivalent what one of the authors explicitly disowns.

AXIS 5 restated at finding level: weakest-subsystem single rating vs per-subsystem class vector. These two rules cannot both describe the same certificate, and translating between them silently loses information.
A certification body's own whitepaper conceding that the standard it certifies against contains no evaluation scheme.

AXIS 7 at finding level: AC4 concedes the maintenance state and says nothing about physical separation; Tier IV requires both tests to hold and requires compartmentalization. Reading them as equivalent overstates AC4 and understates Tier IV's civil cost.
Naming TCDD/TCCF/TCOS and TCDD's two-year validity is the content the gap says is missing.
The withdrawal statement is the falsifier that the 2023-circulated table fails.
Second worked example of an author-withdrawn term still circulating.

'During maintenance activities, the risk of disruption may be elevated' - even at Tier IV.
Tier IV single points of failure listed as 'None + fire and EPO'.
30 minimal cut sets vs 7 at identical 1.8%/yr unreliability - count and probability diverge, and neither is taught.
'The use of static transfer switches in dual path architectures prevents the isolation of both redundant paths.'
The synchroniser is added to make STS transfers safe and in doing so creates an interfaces-class CCCG across every UPS it touches.
A 1-10% mis-cording rate means the as-built graph differs from the as-designed graph continuously.
'48 hours' from two 24-hour tanks is 24 concurrently-maintainable hours.
Three postmortems, three decades, same conclusion: the transfer is the dangerous state.
'an upstream voltage transient affecting both utility power feeds A and B' - the utility must be modelled as a shared disturbance source.
The chillers did not fail; the chiller controller did, and it appears on no power one-line.
Recovery procedures are a procedures-class coupling mechanism; the isolation boundary held under failure and dissolved under human recovery.
The decision cannot be recorded as a topology NAME because the names 'can mean different things to different people'. It must be recorded as a one-line diagram plus a declared CCCG list.
Directionally supportive but UNGROUNDED - only a web-search summary of press releases was seen; the underlying Annual Outage Analysis reports were not read and the 43% figure was not verified.

'The chiller controller dropped offline during the voltage transient event, failing to signal the chilled water distribution pumps to restart.'

NOT a counterexample to N+1 or 2N. It is an antecedent violation: a shared upstream disturbance demanded a simultaneous transfer on both sides (demand correlation), then side A's DRUPS failed. Precision matters - a previous analysis mis-read this as redundancy failing.
'a breaker in front of one of the generators opened' plus 'a second generator independently failed due to a mechanical issue' - two losses in one commanded transfer.
The manual network-device restore introduced a bad configuration that degraded both AZs - the fault crossed the boundary via the recovery action, not the failure.

'each generator independently failed to provide stable voltage as they were brought into service', repeated on the second utility failure - identical behaviour across a group under identical demand is the textbook CCCG signature.
'the UPS systems were depleting and servers began losing power at 8:04pm PDT' - ride-through is a clock, not a redundancy.
Chiller controller, DRUPS transfer control, and the utility breaker's protective logic - all control, none drawn on a power one-line.
CCF definition supplies the antecedent that the redundancy claim leaves unstated.
Teaching the antecedent explicitly is the remedy for the mis-reporting of common-mode events.
The baseline case: 'a series of single points of failure', 7 minimal cut sets in the published PRA. The teaching starting point for cut-set enumeration.
Identical make/model/rating/firmware modules on one shared bus and one shared control is the cleanest teaching instance of design/hardware/function coupling.
N+2 exists precisely to cover the maintenance state; it is unintelligible without state-dependent thinking.
The 30-vs-7 cut-set result at identical unreliability is the acceptance fixture for the whole cut-set curriculum.
'the system has many operating modes and many possible transitions between them. It is difficult to test all of these modes' - the argument for computing class per operating state.
'In 2(N+1) designs, UPS redundancy still exists, even during concurrent maintenance' - the distinguishing property, and the one buyers forget to ask for.
The STS is a decision-making device joining A and B; modelling it as a redundancy node produces wrong cut sets.
The sanctioned remedy for single-corded legacy load: push transfer to the rack rather than onto one large STS.
The published A-alone/B-alone functionality rule and the +/-10% balance rule are the testable content the gap is missing.
'A single panel or single ATS feeding all fuel pumps is a common example' - non-IT ATSs are the ones that silently span both sides.
Fuel has its own topology and its own clock; both are needed to compute time-to-load-loss.
DRUPS relocates rather than removes the transfer risk, and its failure removes ride-through and generation together.

Shorter designed runtime tightens the coupling to generator-start reliability; the BMS adds a control node. Confidence held down because the NFPA 855 specifics behind the room/architecture consequences were not read.
Li-ion room design is governed by NFPA 855, but the standard is paywalled and only a search summary was seen. Do not act on thresholds until the standard or the AHJ confirms them.

Weak link: the busway point is about enclosure-scoped coupling, not control. Emitted at low confidence because no busway-specific source was read; the underlying hardening principle (separate rooms) comes from WP75.
Breaker coordination decides whether a small fault is a 1-rack cut set or a whole-board cut set.
'Two feeds' is the most-taught redundancy and the clearest environment-class CCCG; teaching it correctly teaches the whole concept.
The nine coupling mechanisms with a data-centre instance for each is the missing curriculum unit.
The typed graph plus required outputs is the executable form of the missing skill; it is the cdcp_plant specification.
Control node kind exists specifically so EPO, fire alarm and BMS sequences enter the cut-set computation.
CCCGs are not derivable from the feeds-graph. Without the overlay the model systematically OVERSTATES resilience.
Acceptance fixture: the model must reproduce 30-vs-7 cut sets at equal unreliability, or it is not modelling complexity cost.
'With the advent of dual-cord capable IT equipment, these devices along with their undesirable failure modes can be eliminated with a significant increase in system availability.'

In the STS variants: 'Design relies on the proper operation of the STS equipment which represents single points of failure and complex failure modes'. The tri-redundant variant removes this dependency by requiring 100% dual-corded load.
'Allows for concurrent maintenance of all components if all loads are dual-corded' - the guarantee is conditional on the cord map.
'tier IV power architectures require that all loads are dual-corded, including electrical feeds to air conditioning equipment.'
'Two or more primary modules need a special circuit to enable selection of the reserve module or the utility as the bypass source (static transfer switch)'.
The pattern's guarantee is bounded by the shared bus, board and controls.

Uptime's public journal states 12 hours minimum at design load for Tier III/IV with concurrently-maintainable or fault-tolerant supply AND return paths. No clause number asserted; the standard was not read.
If Uptime certification is the target, the electrical decision cannot be taken independently of the mechanical topology - the site rating is the weakest subsystem.
The decision must state which of the two properties is required, over which event class, in which operating states. A level name does not encode this.
Until the target document, body and lifecycle stage are named, the class decision is unstatable - 'Tier 3' has at least six meanings in this market.

AXIS: curve shape and stated test conditions. The trade claim asserts a single linear rate; Dell's instrumented data shows a steep first regime set by aisle air inventory, an inflection, then a slower linear regime — and the rate differs by density, room volume, containment and whether air movers are running. The trade figures state none of those conditions.

AXIS: which plant is being measured, and which failure the lever acts on. Cundall ranks thermal storage above UPS-on-pumps for a CHILLED WATER network under total utility loss (the water side is what warms). Dell ranks UPS-on-fans first for an AIR-SIDE failure at 350 W/sq ft (the air side is what stops). The two are not competing answers to one question; treating them as a single ranking is how a design ends up buying only one of them. Also a 15-year date gap (2011 vs 2026) and a large density gap.

AXIS: which failure you optimise against, at the same architectural choice. Schneider credits rack-mounted CDUs with 'limits potential failure modes to a single rack' AND penalises them for 'short thermal ride through'; floor-mounted CDUs invert both. Minimising blast radius and maximising ride-through are directly opposed at the CDU form-factor decision, and the same document argues both sides without resolving them.

AXIS: practitioner risk perception versus technical assessment, within a single document. LBNL states 'data center professionals are split in the perception of risk' and simultaneously that with MERV 13 'the negative effects of outside air pollutants are small'. The disagreement is not between two measurements — it is between a measurement and an industry's willingness to act on it, which means it will not be resolved by more measurement.

AXIS: modelled optimal operation versus reported actual operation, same cooling system type. LBNL's simulation assumes adiabatic assist is 'not used most of the year'; operators of similar plant report 0.1-0.3 L/kWh, which LBNL concedes is 'much higher than the values simulated here'. Using the modelled figure for a water budget understates demand by the difference between designed intent and operating practice.

AXIS: which inventory the heat capacity is measured against. The standard argument for liquid is that water carries far more heat than air; Cundall's finding is that liquid-cooled systems 'tend to have lower thermal inertia' because the load scales faster than the coolant inventory. Both statements are true at different levels of aggregation — per unit mass of coolant versus per kW of load — and only the second one predicts survival time.

AXIS: what the limit is FOR. Dell states its systems 'typically will not hit a shutdown trigger point until at least 10C (18F) past the maximum allowable temperature' and that short excursions have 'no measurable effect on long-term reliability', while other vendors 'may have default shutdown limits that are lower'. The envelope standard defines a reliability/warranty band; the vendor firmware defines an availability cliff. Designing ride-through to the envelope limit over-buys for some fleets and under-buys for others. NOTE: no envelope values are asserted here.

AXIS: whose clock governs. The same whitepaper assigns facility-side thermal measurement at once per 60 s and IT-side node/component measurement at once per second, then declares the layer between them 'negotiated'. The fast data exists on the IT side of an ownership boundary that has no default, so the facility protection loop is slow by construction, not by choice.

AXIS: the density at which a resilience feature becomes mandatory versus the Tier at which it is required. Continuous cooling is formally a Tier IV requirement, but the same source recommends it above 4 kW/rack 'regardless of Tier' — a threshold roughly an order of magnitude below planned AI densities. So a Tier III campus at 100 kW/rack is outside the recommendation while being inside the standard. The Tier label and the physics disagree, and the Tier Standard text is paywalled and unread, so the disagreement cannot be resolved from open sources.

AXIS: as-installed versus as-operated, over time. Dell measures containment's ride-through benefit on a purpose-built sealed rack in a lab; NERSC reports that in service containment requires manual adjustment during heat events, leaks at panel and rack gaps, and is 'difficult to balance with IT equipment maintenance & reconfigurations'. The resilience credit is real at handover and decays on a schedule nobody measures.
CONVERGENCE with wave-1 L3: L3 recorded the chiller-controller quote from the electrical side; this lineage adds a second independent operator incident (Azure Australia East) with the same shape.

Not the same event — the same FAILURE PATTERN: utility voltage disturbance, mechanically healthy plant, control/signalling path lost, cooling not restored, IT load shed. Recorded as duplicates at the pattern level so the two incidents are analysed as one class.
CONVERGENCE with wave-1 L3: mechanical controllers and their power sources are a common-cause component group that crosses the electrical/mechanical boundary.
CONVERGENCE with wave-1 L3: the cut-set model must be extended with cooling components, their controllers, and controller power, or it will score N+2 chiller plant as fault tolerant when it is not.

CONVERGENCE with wave-1 L3: chiller restart cannot begin until the generator has accepted load. Dell: 'the generator should be started as soon as possible to get air movement around the room'. Generator start time is therefore a term in the thermal budget, not only the electrical one.
CONVERGENCE with wave-1 L6: the emergency power system's classified start/transfer time is an input to the thermal ride-through budget. NFPA 110 was NOT read; no clause or class is asserted.
CONVERGENCE with wave-1 L6: same pattern — make the number a bid-responsiveness requirement so it is disclosed before award rather than discovered at commissioning.
CONVERGENCE with wave-1 L6: FAT proves the machine, IST proves the plant. A CDU or chiller that passed FAT can still fail the integrated restart sequence; neither test substitutes for the other.

CONVERGENCE with wave-1 L6: the refrigerant install deadline interacts with equipment lead time. A chiller with a 2-year lead time ordered against a pre-deadline design arrives after the installation prohibition takes effect.
CONVERGENCE with wave-1 L3: the resilience-class target constrains the cooling topology through the continuous cooling requirement. The Tier Standard text is paywalled and was not read.
CONVERGENCE point: the plain canonical UPS label is used deliberately so this merges with any other lineage's UPS node rather than forking on a qualifier.

Named by convention as the product/process certification accreditation standard; text not opened

AXIS: validity period of a design-stage conformity award. Same object class (a review of drawings against a resilience classification), two schemes, two different clocks - Uptime TCDD expires 2 years after award; ANSI/TIA-942 Design is valid 1 year (extendable while the facility is non-operational). A buyer treating Tier III and Rated-3 as interchangeable inherits a 2x difference in how fast the paper decays.

AXIS: whether a constructed-facility award decays and requires ongoing surveillance. ANSI/TIA-942 Facilities is valid 3 years with mandatory surveillance audits at years 1 and 2 and recertification at year 3. Uptime publishes no expiry for Tier Certification of Constructed Facility on the page read. Not a disagreement about the building - a disagreement about whether a constructed-facility attestation is a point-in-time fact or a maintained state.

AXIS: independence of the conformity assessment body from the standard owner. TIA owns the standard and licenses SEPARATE Certification Bodies evaluated against ISO/IEC 17020/17021 for 'impartiality, competency, and consistency', and forbids individual auditors. Uptime Institute owns the standard and issues the awards itself, with no external accreditation body named on any page read. Both are coherent; they are not the same kind of assurance and should not be priced as if they were.

AXIS: the meaning of the word 'accreditation'. EPI states its courses have 'an impartial accreditation and examination from EXIN' - an exam-institute delivery relationship. ISO/IEC 17024 accreditation means a national accreditation body peer-evaluated a personnel-certification body and admitted it to a multilateral recognition arrangement. No 17024 claim appears on exin.com or exin.com/about-exin/ (which state only 'ISO 27001 certified', a claim about EXIN's own information security). The statement is not false; the word does two jobs and the reader cannot tell which.

AXIS: the OBJECT of accreditation - organisation versus document versus facility. TIA writes that ANSI/TIA-942 is 'Accredited by ANSI'. ANSI accredits standards DEVELOPERS and APPROVES documents as American National Standards; it accredits neither documents nor data centres. TIA's underlying status is correct and the compression is the direct source of the downstream 'ANSI accredited data centre' error.

AXIS: self-declaration versus awarded conformity. 'Tier III' as used in marketing names no award, no issuer, no date and no register entry, and is applied indiscriminately to TCDD-only facilities, to Tier Gap Analysis outputs that carry no award at all, and to sites deploying Tier-Ready modular products. The Uptime programme distinguishes five distinct products. The market collapses them into one adjective.

AXIS: role separation within a single scheme. EPI authors DCOS (a competing operations standard it also certifies against), trains the TIA-942 auditors (CTDC/CTIA/CTLA), has its exams run by EXIN, AND operates as one of eight TIA-licensed Certification Bodies issuing TIA-942 certificates. The scheme's own licensing basis (ISO/IEC 17020/17021) exists to manage exactly this concentration. Disclosed, permitted, and materially different from a CB with a single role.

AXIS: whose credential defines competence in a scheme. TIA's consultants-and-auditors guidance points at CTDC - a proprietary training credential owned by EPI, one of TIA's own licensed CBs - as the qualification a TIA-942 consultant should hold. The scheme owner is deferring to a commercial credential held by a participant in its own scheme.

AXIS: vendor neutrality of data-centre education, before versus after 2023. CNet was the market's independent training provider; since the 2023 acquisition it is 'an Uptime Education Company'. Uptime therefore owns the Tier Standard, issues Tier awards, endorses ATD/ATS/AOS holders, AND sells BTEC-backed credentials competing with EPI's. Any guidance describing CNet as a neutral alternative to Uptime is stale.

AXIS: who issues the credential and whether it is legally operative. 'NFPA 70E certified' implies an NFPA-issued worker credential enforcing a legal requirement. OSHA has NOT adopted NFPA 70E - it 'can be used by employers as guides' and functions as General Duty Clause evidence that a hazard is 'recognized'. The enforceable object is OSHA's qualified-person determination, documented by the employer, not a vendor attendance certificate.

AXIS: formal standing of a standard - process emulation versus consensus approval. DCOS is 'prepared by a committee under the leadership of EPI following strict ISO/ANSI standard development processes'. ANSI/TIA-942 is an ANSI-approved American National Standard from an ANSI-accredited developer. 'Developed like a consensus standard' and 'is a consensus standard' are different claims that read identically to a buyer.

AXIS: temporal validity of the accreditation-recognition framework itself. IAF 'ceased operations on 01 January 2026' and was replaced by Global Accreditation Cooperation Incorporated. Every curriculum, RFP template and compliance procedure naming 'the IAF MLA' as the current mechanism is out of date, and the post-transition custodianship of IAF CertSearch is unconfirmed.

AXIS: level of assembly at which conformity was assessed - manufacturer product versus deployed site. Tier-Ready pre-validates a modular manufacturer's design and 'reduces end-user's Tier Certification time by 65%'. It does not attest anything about the site the product lands on. TCCF attests the constructed facility under 'live system demonstrations under real-world conditions'.

AXIS: same level-of-assembly split inside the TIA scheme, with a validity twist. Ready certifies that 'a modular data center has been designed in accordance to the ANSI/TIA-942 standard' and is valid 1 year with yearly recertification; Facilities requires physical onsite inspection and runs 3 years with surveillance. A 'TIA-942 certified' modular product is a design attestation on a 12-month clock, not an inspected facility.

AXIS: whether an operations assessment is gated on the Tier award ladder. M&O criteria identify behaviours 'independent of Tiers and the installed infrastructure' and require no Tier award. TCOS requires BOTH Tier Certification of Design Documents and Tier Certification of Constructed Facility first. Two Uptime operations products, both derived from the Tier Standard: Operational Sustainability, with incompatible prerequisites and different meanings in a data room.

AXIS: whether an engagement produces an award. A Tier Gap Analysis delivers 'the same review as is done in the first pass review of a Tier Standard of Topology Design Documents Certification service' - same reviewers, same first pass, same letterhead - and produces a deficiency report with no Tier designation. In an evidence pack a TGA report and a TCDD award are near-indistinguishable and mean opposite things.

AXIS: whether a state-issued professional licence gates the credential. ATD 'is open to licensed professional engineers'; ATS 'does not require a licensed credential'. Same issuer, same 16-hour format, same US$4,985 price, same 'Uptime Accredited' branding. A staffing requirement written as 'Uptime accredited' is satisfied by the unlicensed one.

AXIS: whether a certificate carries accredited assurance. Accredited certification bodies undergo 'stringent evaluation of their operations by a peer evaluation team'; unaccredited ones do not, and both issue certificates that look the same. The distinction is invisible on the document and resolvable only in an accreditation body's register.

AXIS: whose approval a historical certificate carries. TIA states that prior to the licensed-CB scheme 'many companies in the industry' audited to TIA-942 'without oversight from TIA' with accuracy that 'varied', and that going forward only licensed-CB audits 'will be approved by TIA'. A large installed base of TIA-942 certificates therefore exists that the standard's owner does not stand behind.

AXIS: recorded_at only. Wood Mackenzie Q2 2025 = 128 weeks; VAWN 2026-08-13 = 160+ and elevating. Same item, ~+25% in about a year. This is the canonical demonstration that lead times must be dated.

AXIS 1: recorded_at (Wood Mackenzie Q2 2025 vs Terrapin 2026-06-10). AXIS 2: aggregation level - national all-industry index vs data-centre-specific metal-clad configurations. Not independent sources: VAWN's methodology lists Wood Mackenzie as an input.

AXIS: order posture. 40-80 weeks is a catalogue quote for a new order placed normally; ~150 weeks is a replacement demanded late into a saturated order book. The second number should size the risk reserve, the first the base schedule. Chateau's publication year is not stated, lowering confidence.
Two independently authored 2026 sources (2026-05-06 and 2026-06-10) whose ranges overlap substantially, both far above the index figure.

AXIS: statistic type. An all-equipment global MEAN (33 weeks) against a single critical-path MAXIMUM (160+ weeks). Both true; only the maximum is a valid schedule input. The average is the most dangerous number in the dataset because it is quotable and reassuring.

SELF-CONTRADICTION within one source: a 16-24 week catalogue lead time stated alongside a supply chain sized for 5-8 GW/yr facing 17+ GW/yr demand. AXIS: catalogue figure assumes available capacity the same document denies exists. Instructive because it shows how catalogue figures are generated.

AXIS: cause. Manufacturing capacity shortfall (Wood Mackenzie) vs procurement practice, vendor qualification rules and utility hierarchies inflating apparent scarcity (Tarver, Bolt Electrical). Both positions appear in the same 2026-01-02 article. Operationally decisive: remedy is money-and-time under one, buyer-behaviour under the other.

Component-level queues (bushings 130 wk, OLTC 80-90 wk) are hard to explain as buyer-side procurement behaviour, so they weigh toward a genuine capacity constraint - though they do not exclude over-specification as a contributing cause.

AXIS: whose schedule is being described. The supplier calls it 'minor' and 'temporary' (2026-07-29); owners and their advisers call the same period the binding constraint on 30-50% of 2026 capacity (2026-04-08). A quarter of supplier revenue slip is a year of owner energisation slip.

AXIS: verifiability, not substance. The specific 'Cummins sold out through 2028' year could not be traced to any primary Cummins statement; what IS sourced is Caterpillar's $63bn Q1 2026 backlog and commentary expecting suppliers sold out 1-3 years. Recorded so downstream agents reject the unverifiable figure rather than re-deriving it.

AXIS: contractual allocation vs commercial reality. The clean EPC/EPCM risk split holds on paper; 2024-2026 practice shows EPC contractors negotiating equipment-unavailability carve-outs and re-baselining, so the allocation does not survive contact with uninsurable supply risk.
The sequencing rule exists because interconnection is itself a 12-36 month process; run in series with equipment it doubles the campus timeline.
The 160+ week transformer is the reason the two clocks cannot be run sequentially.

SCHEDULE DEPENDENCY: transformer delivery gates grid energisation, which gates commissioning and revenue. Sightline Climate names transformers as the cause of the 30-50% slip because there is no substitute on a shorter lead time.
SCHEDULE DEPENDENCY: MV switchgear is the second gate. Even where a transformer arrives, the lineup it feeds must exist before energisation and commissioning can proceed.
SCHEDULE DEPENDENCY: the standby system cannot be commissioned on generator delivery alone; the paralleling switchgear (52-104 wk) outlasts the gensets (50-78 wk) and is the true milestone.
SCHEDULE DEPENDENCY beneath the assembly: bushings (130 wk) and OLTCs (80-90 wk) are separately queued sub-components that set the transformer's floor and explain refused expedites.
Announced capacity comes online in 2027, after the month-one 2026 decision. Announcements do not shorten an existing queue.
80% import dependence plus a 50% copper duty means the longest-queue item is also the most trade-policy-exposed.

AXIS: electrical state of the plant at the same level number. anvilfield's Level 3 is de-energised ('installed, terminated, meggered, and ready to energize' - megger testing requires a dead system); FST, constructandcommission, CxPlanner and DataX Connect all place witnessed start-up and energisation at Level 3. A specification saying 'Level 3 complete' does not say whether the switchgear is live.

AXIS: which level is the integration boundary - an off-by-one. Majority: Level 4 is each system alone under fault, Level 5 is the first integrated test at design load. stelic: Level 4 is 'systems tested together, under simulated failure scenarios' and Level 5 is performance 'once it is fully populated with IT load' - a POST-OCCUPANCY test, which makes a contract gating IT delivery on 'Level 5' circular.

AXIS: whether handover is inside the commissioning scheme. constructandcommission makes closeout/turnover/handover Level 6, i.e. a witnessed Cx deliverable with a signatory; DataX Connect and CxPlanner end at Level 5, making handover contract administration that nobody signs for.

AXIS: whether a level is a one-time gate or a repeatable depth of verification. Every trade scheme treats Level 1 as done once at the factory. Uptime Institute instructs 'Repeat Level 1 procedures in the actual data center environment since factory witness testing is performed in ideal conditions rarely seen in practice'. The commercial consequence: repeat-on-site is not in the default bid.

AXIS: the SIGN of the reactive component the test must present. Walt Power specifies inductive lagging at 0.8 PF (the generator nameplate point, matching motor-dominated mechanical load); Crestchic sells capacitive load banks for 'the leading power factor often associated with servers'. One test cannot cover both signs, and the facility contains both loads on different buses.

AXIS: whether the alternator's excitation and voltage-regulation behaviour is inside the acceptance scope. Resistive-only holds PF 1.0 and tests kW; the same vendor states a resistive test does not validate 'voltage stability', 'AVR performance' or 'excitation response' and 'a generator that passes a resistive test may still perform poorly under real inductive loads'. Resistive-only is nonetheless the default meaning of 'load bank test' in specifications.

AXIS: whether independence is a contractual arrangement or a personal qualification. AABC Commissioning Group: 'an independent, certified, commissioning authority UNDER CONTRACT TO THE OWNER is the preferred contractual arrangement'. GSA's Desired Qualifications page - experience, HVAC/EMCS, TAB, codes, degree preference - never mentions independence, and its selection page treats the CA as an ordinary professional service. GSA's silence is safe only because GSA is itself the contracting owner; copied into a GC-led private RFP it produces a qualified CxA with no stated allegiance.

AXIS: process model, and therefore what the word 'commissioning' denotes. GSA structures commissioning as owner LIFECYCLE STAGES (Planning/Design/Construction/Post-construction) answering 'whose process and when', with the Cx record turned over BEFORE substantial completion. The data-centre schemes structure it as numbered TEST-DEPTH LEVELS answering 'how deep and who signs', with the IST at or after substantial completion. They are orthogonal, not competing, and each is incomplete alone.

AXIS: which authority owns the term 'integrated testing', who signs it, and on what recurrence. CxA for the owner, once, before IT load (Level 5 IST) versus integrated testing agent for the AHJ, before certificate of occupancy and periodically thereafter (NFPA 4). Same building, same emergency power system, same HVAC/smoke-control interface, two unreconciled test regimes.

AXIS: scope + building type + date, not measurement error. GSA's 0.5-1.5 percent is COMMISSIONING AGENT FEES for conventional federal buildings (guide vintage pre-2010, GSA's own practice about 0.5 percent). The 2026 data-centre figure of 0.75-3.0 percent folds in load bank rental, trade standby labour during the IST and a 10-25 percent re-test contingency. Comparing the percentages directly is a category error.

AXIS: certification scope. A tier certificate is a claim about documented or constructed topology; the failure was in the operating configuration in force on the night (utility and generation run in parallel for a grid-services programme). Not a disagreement about facts - a disagreement about what the certificate covers.

AXIS: which standard governs which hazard. Industry practice cites 1910.147 as the data-centre electrical LOTO authority; 1910.147(a)(1)(ii)(D) excludes exactly that exposure and assigns it to Subpart S. The conflict is one of scope, not of content.

AXIS: whether an IT load is 'a continuous industrial process'. The default rule and the infeasibility example point opposite ways for data-centre work, and no public OSHA interpretation reachable in this pass settles the definitional question.

AXIS: basis of interval and unit of analysis. Vendor intervals are set against a warranty-liability envelope for an individual serial number; the failure-pattern evidence is a population distribution. The two disagree by construction, not by error.

edges.note: AXIS: consequence class and the regulatory regime that follows. Control designs transfer from nuclear and aviation; loss-of-life consequence and statutory enforcement do not. Overclaiming equivalence was explicitly rejected in prior review.

AXIS: what is counted and for whom. DCIM/BMS scope and price are set by monitored point count, which the integrator can quantify; alarm quality is measured in operator-actionable alarms per operator per hour. The two metrics move in opposite directions and the procurement one wins by default.
AXIS: jurisdiction and applicability, not the numbers. The limits are explicit and defensible; they bind NRC licensees only, and no equivalent binds this sector.

AXIS: evidentiary status, not magnitude. The figure may well be correct; it is not verifiable from any source readable under rule 2, and repetition across L6 and L9 is circulation rather than corroboration.

AXIS: purpose and audience of the record. A blameless learning document and a contractual/regulatory record want different attribution and different precision about who did what and when; one artefact cannot serve both without degrading.
AXIS: layer of verification. Process liveness and end-to-end function are different observables; the 2003 case turns entirely on a team accepting the former as evidence of the latter.

AXIS: independence assumption. Redundant monitoring nodes are independent in hardware and dependent in application state; N+1 counts boxes, and the failure crossed the boundary the count does not model.
AXIS: whose account. Every PDX-04 characterisation of the facility operator's actions is one party's narrative; the operator's public response returned 403 and is absent from this graph.
